title: Ravi Vakil on Mathematical Writing
note: Ravi Vakil on Mathematical Writing. Advice and guidance about how to write mathematics clearly and effectively. The page also gives his reflections on this subject.

title: Adelic and Classical Modular Forms for GL(2)
note: Adelic and Classical Modular Forms for GL(2). An exposition of the translation between classical modular forms and automorphic forms on the adelic group $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$. It gives a geometric interpretation of modular forms as sections of line bundles over modular curves. It also gives minimal ad hoc constructions of Eisenstein series. It gives the details of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb{R})$ with basis elements $Z, H, Y_+, Y_-$. The center $\mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ of the universal enveloping algebra is isomorphic to a polynomial ring in two generators. It examines the space of bases $B$ of $\mathbb{C}$ as a real vector space. This space is an open subset of $\mathbb{C}^2$ with commuting left and right actions by $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathbb{C})$. The right action of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is complex analytic. It gives an identification with the upper half-plane $\mathcal{H}^{\pm} \times \mathbb{C}^\times$ through $(\tau, z) \mapsto \left(\frac{a\tau+c}{b\tau+d}, (b\tau+d)z\right)$. It examines the decomposition of the complexified Lie algebra tangent space into holomorphic and anti-holomorphic subspaces. It also examines the subspace $V_i \subset \mathfrak{gl}_2$, and the bijection $B/\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathcal{L}$ with the moduli of discrete rank-2 lattices. It includes moderate growth conditions, smooth adelic automorphic forms, and representations invariant under right translation by $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_f)$.

title: Deligne on Modular Forms
note: Deligne on Modular Forms. Notes by Pierre Deligne that give the foundations of the algebraic and geometric theory of modular forms. Emerton's notes refer to them.

title: Alex Youcis
note: Alex Youcis, Motivation behind Shimura Varieties. This is the first post in a series about Shimura varieties. It gives a broad motivation for the subject. It tells why Shimura varieties are natural to study, and what they give.

title: Algebraic Geometry and Arithmetic Duality
note: Algebraic Geometry and Arithmetic Duality. It connects the eigenvalues of the Frobenius action on étale cohomology $H_{\text{ét}}^*(X, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ to the zeros and poles of zeta functions. Thus it completes the arithmetic dictionary through the adèle class space.

title: Class Field Theory and Noncommutative Geometry
note: Class Field Theory and Noncommutative Geometry. An exposition by Alain Connes on class field theory through the adèle class space $X_{\mathbb{Q}} = \mathbb{Q}^\times \backslash \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}}$. The idele class group $C_K = \mathbb{A}_K^\times / K^\times$ of a number field $K$ encodes the abelian extensions of the field internally. Through Artin reciprocity, this group acts as a Galois group of the maximal abelian extension. Group actions on spaces give the Galois actions on roots. The quotient space $X_K = K^\times \backslash \mathbb{A}_K$ is ergodic with respect to the Haar measure. Thus it is a prototype noncommutative space (leaf space of a foliation). The text translates local-to-global class field theory through the inclusion of local isotropy groups $K_v^\times \hookrightarrow C_K$. It connects the Riemann–Weil explicit formulas $\sum_v \int f(u)/|1-u|\,d^*u$ to a trace formula for the scaling operator on the adèle class space. It introduces the scaling site $X_{\mathbb{Q}} = \mathbb{Q}^\times \backslash \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}} / \widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^\times$. Its model is a noncommutative space of rank-1 subgroups of $\mathbb{R}$. In this space, periodic orbits of length $\log p$ agree with prime numbers $p$, and the Frobenius endomorphism is a mapping torus. The text relates this construction to Grothendieck's étale fundamental group $\pi_1^{\text{ét}}$ and the 3D topology of $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}$.

title: Overview of O-Minimality
note: Overview of O-Minimality. Scanlon's survey on o-minimal structures, tame topology, and their applications in model theory and arithmetic geometry.

title: Maximal Abelian Extensions Unramified Outside S
note: Maximal Abelian Extensions Unramified Outside S. A discussion and calculation of the maximal abelian extension $K_S^{\text{ab}}$ of a number field $K$ unramified outside a finite set of places $S$. For a singleton prime $S = \{p\}$, the direct limit of ray class fields modulo $\mathfrak{p}^n \mathcal{O}_K$ gives $K_S^{\text{ab}}$. The thread tells about ramification at infinite places and the Galois group $G_S(K)^{\text{ab}} = G_S(K) / \overline{[G_S(K), G_S(K)]}$. It gives the details of the connection to class field theory, Poitou–Tate duality, and the Kronecker–Weber theorem for $K = \mathbb{Q}$.

title: Direct Proof of the Kronecker-Weber Theorem
note: Direct Proof of the Kronecker-Weber Theorem. Lemmermeyer's direct proof that a cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_m)$ contains each finite abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$.

title: Ergodicity of Global Fields on Adeles
note: Ergodicity of Global Fields on Adeles. A rigorous proof of the ergodicity of the action of $K^\times$ on the adèle ring $\mathbb{A}_K$ for global fields. The proof applies to the number field setting and to the function field setting.

title: Perspectives on Reciprocity Laws
note: Perspectives on Reciprocity Laws. Emerton's survey on reciprocity from Gauss's quadratic reciprocity to Langlands functoriality. It compares Dirichlet's analytic class number formula for $L(1, \chi)$ (automorphic side) with Dedekind's class number formula (motivic side). It also discusses the Sato–Tate conjecture.

title: Categorical p-Adic Langlands Correspondence
note: Categorical p-Adic Langlands Correspondence. A complete 252-page treatise by Emerton and Helm. It gives the formulation of the categorical $p$-adic Langlands program in the Banach setting and in the rigid analytic setting.

title: Reductive Group Schemes after SGA3
note: Reductive Group Schemes after SGA3. Brian Conrad's notes on the foundations of the theory and classification of reductive group schemes over general bases.

title: Research Remarks by Matthew Emerton
note: Research Remarks by Matthew Emerton. A collection of notes, papers, and essays by Matthew Emerton on automorphic forms, Galois representations, and the Langlands program.

title: Fourier Analysis vs Representation Theory
note: Fourier Analysis vs Representation Theory. Discussion on the relation between harmonic analysis and group representations. It shows the Peter–Weyl theorem for compact groups $G$, which decomposes $L^2(G) \cong \widehat{\bigoplus}_{\pi} V_\pi \otimes V_\pi^*$. It also shows the Plancherel decomposition for non-compact type I groups through Harish-Chandra's work.

title: Harmonic Analysis and Physics
note: Harmonic Analysis and Physics. Survey of Plancherel decompositions on reductive Lie groups. It also gives Bargmann's classification of irreducible unitary representations of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$, with physical applications.

title: Conceptual Meaning of the Weil Conjectures
note: Conceptual Meaning of the Weil Conjectures. Discussion on the philosophical and geometric requirements for a proof of the Weil conjectures. The requirements include Weil cohomology theories, standard conjectures, and motives.

title: Shimura's Problem and Class Field Theory
note: Shimura's Problem and Class Field Theory. It examines the connection between polynomial splitting fields, ray class groups, and complex multiplication. Example: the splitting of polynomials that generate abelian extensions inside cyclotomic fields such as $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7)$.

title: Geometric Realization of Galois Representations
note: Geometric Realization of Galois Representations. The 2-dimensional Galois representations attached to modular forms occur inside the étale cohomology $H^1_{\text{ét}}(X_0(N)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ of modular curves. This realization leads to Shimura varieties.

title: The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
note: The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology. Atiyah and Bott's foundational paper on the de Rham localization theorem in equivariant cohomology $H_G^*(M)$. It links Hamiltonian group actions, moment maps $\mu: M \to \mathfrak{g}^*$, symplectic reduction, and the Duistermaat–Heckman exact stationary phase formula. It connects equivariant localization to moduli spaces of bundles on Riemann surfaces and to Yang–Mills theory.

title: Atiyah-Bott Localization in Geometry
note: Atiyah-Bott Localization in Geometry. Jae Hee Lee's expository REU paper. It gives the details of the Atiyah–Bott localization theorem, equivariant characteristic classes, and topological invariants of quotient manifolds.

title: Moment Maps and Diffeomorphisms in Gauge Theory
note: Moment Maps and Diffeomorphisms in Gauge Theory. Donaldson's paper interprets the curvature of a connection on a surface principal bundle as a moment map for the gauge group action. The paper applies this to the Yang–Mills equations.

title: Convex Body Geometry by Keith Ball
note: Convex Body Geometry by Keith Ball. A complete introduction to convex geometry. It includes the volume calculation of Euclidean balls, the Hahn–Banach separation theorem, and extremal properties of polytopes and cubes.

title: Non-Perturbative BV Theory via Derived Geometry
note: Non-Perturbative BV Theory via Derived Geometry. A formulation of non-perturbative Batalin–Vilkovisky (BV) quantization in derived differential geometry and shifted symplectic structures.

title: Grothendieck's Tohoku Paper
note: Grothendieck's Tohoku Paper. Michael Barr's commentary on Grothendieck's landmark 1957 paper. That paper introduced abelian categories, derived functors $R^i F$, injective resolutions, sheaf cohomology, and the Grothendieck spectral sequence. It gives the foundations for Serre duality and for Ext functors of sheaves.

title: Lectures on Serre's Modular Invariance Conjectures
note: Lectures on Serre's Modular Invariance Conjectures. Ribet and Stein's exposition on Serre's modularity conjecture. The conjecture links odd, irreducible Galois representations $\rho: \operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}) \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ to modular forms of a specified weight and level.

title: Injective Resolutions in Sheaf Cohomology
note: Injective Resolutions in Sheaf Cohomology. A comparison of two methods to calculate sheaf cohomology. One method uses acyclic resolutions (e.g., flasque, soft, fine, or Čech on affine covers). The other method uses universal injective resolutions.

title: Nilpotent Connections and Picard-Fuchs Equations
note: Nilpotent Connections and Picard-Fuchs Equations. Nick Katz's classic paper on regular singular differential equations, Gauss–Manin connections, and $p$-adic nilpotence.

title: Serre's Faisceaux Algébriques Cohérents (FAC)
note: Serre's Faisceaux Algébriques Cohérents (FAC). An annotated translation of Serre's 1955 paper. The paper starts the theory of coherent sheaves $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules and Čech cohomology on algebraic varieties under the Zariski topology.

title: Transversality of a General Translate
note: Transversality of a General Translate. Kleiman's 12-page paper on the transversality of general translates in Schubert calculus and enumerative geometry. It applies over algebraically closed fields in characteristic zero.

title: Introduction to Nonlinear PDEs
note: Introduction to Nonlinear PDEs. Sergiu Klainerman's complete 72-page introduction to modern nonlinear wave equations and evolutionary PDEs.

title: Brill-Noether Theory on K3 Surfaces
note: Brill-Noether Theory on K3 Surfaces. Robert Lazarsfeld's 10-page proof of the Brill–Noether theorem and Gieseker's theorem. The proof uses vector bundles on $K3$ surfaces with $\operatorname{Pic}(X) \cong \mathbb{Z}$.

title: Enumerative Geometry of Moduli Spaces of Curves
note: Enumerative Geometry of Moduli Spaces of Curves. David Mumford's 58-page paper. It makes the Chow ring $A^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g)$ of the moduli space of stable curves, and it gives the definition of the tautological classes $\kappa_i, \psi_i, \lambda_i$. Then it applies Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch.

title: Serre's GAGA Translation
note: Serre's GAGA Translation. An English translation of Serre's 1956 paper Géométrie Algébrique et Géométrie Analytique. The paper shows the equivalence between algebraic coherent sheaves and analytic coherent sheaves on projective complex varieties.

title: Terence Tao's Harmonic Analysis Notes
note: Terence Tao's Harmonic Analysis Notes. Course materials about Calderón–Zygmund theory, interpolation, singular integrals, and oscillatory integrals.

title: Calderon-Zygmund-Stein Theory
note: Calderon-Zygmund-Stein Theory. Tao's notes on classical Calderón–Zygmund theory, kernel estimates, and singular integral bounds on $L^p$ spaces.

title: Complex and Real Interpolation
note: Complex and Real Interpolation. Exposition of the Riesz–Thorin complex interpolation theorem, Marcinkiewicz real interpolation, and bounds on linear operators.

title: Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Inequality
note: Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Inequality. A detailed examination of the Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator $Mf(x)$, weak $(1,1)$ bounds, and $L^p$ maximal inequalities.

title: The Hilbert Transform
note: The Hilbert Transform. The theory of the Hilbert transform, of singular integral operators that fail on the diagonal, and of principal value integrals.

title: Weighted Norm Inequalities
note: Weighted Norm Inequalities. Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weights, weighted $L^p$ estimates, and the boundedness of maximal operators.

title: Introduction to Fourier Summation
note: Introduction to Fourier Summation. It uses the convergence of Fourier series and $L^p$ norm interpolation between extreme bounds as the motivation for harmonic analysis.

title: Paraproducts and Bilinear Operators
note: Paraproducts and Bilinear Operators. An analysis of multilinear operators, Coifman–Meyer paraproducts, and pointwise nonlinear estimates.

title: The T(1) Theorem
note: The T(1) Theorem. David and Journé's $T(1)$ theorem for the $L^2$-boundedness of non-convolution Calderón–Zygmund operators. The proof uses paraproducts and BMO estimates.

title: Oscillatory Integrals
note: Oscillatory Integrals. Stationary phase methods, the van der Corput lemma, and the asymptotic estimation of oscillatory integrals.

title: Harmonic Analysis on Finite Abelian Groups
note: Harmonic Analysis on Finite Abelian Groups. Discrete Fourier transforms, Pontryagin duality for finite groups, and convolution identities. In this finite setting, there are no measure-theoretic difficulties.

title: Representation Theory of Finite Non-Abelian Groups
note: Representation Theory of Finite Non-Abelian Groups. Noncommutative harmonic analysis, character theory, matrix coefficients, and Fourier inversion for finite non-abelian groups.

title: Advanced Harmonic Analysis
note: Advanced Harmonic Analysis. A course archive about Littlewood–Paley theory, BMO spaces, and the methods of dispersive PDE.

title: Tate's Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves
note: Tate's Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves. Henri Darmon's notes, which come from Tate's classic lectures on elliptic curves, group laws, and formal groups.

title: Number Theoretic Background for Tate's Thesis
note: Number Theoretic Background for Tate's Thesis. Claus Sorensen's notes on local fields, Haar measures, and Tate's Fourier-analytic reformulation of zeta functions.

title: Supersymmetry and Morse Theory
note: Supersymmetry and Morse Theory. Edward Witten's paper derives the Morse inequalities through perturbations $d_t = e^{-th} d e^{th}$ of the de Rham complex and supersymmetric quantum mechanics.

title: Equidistribution and the Bogomolov Conjecture
note: Equidistribution and the Bogomolov Conjecture. Shou-Wu Zhang's paper proves the Bogomolov conjecture for curves through arithmetic intersection theory and Arakelov heights.

title: Characteristic Classes by Milnor and Stasheff
note: Characteristic Classes by Milnor and Stasheff. A classic textbook on vector bundles, Stiefel–Whitney classes, Chern classes, Pontryagin classes, and the Euler class.

title: Morse Theory by John Milnor
note: Morse Theory by John Milnor. A classic text on critical point theory, handlebody attachments, and the topology of smooth manifolds.

title: Topology from the Differentiable Viewpoint
note: Topology from the Differentiable Viewpoint. Milnor's text about smooth maps, regular values, Sard's theorem, Brouwer degree, and the Hopf degree theorem.

title: Serre's A Course in Arithmetic
note: Serre's A Course in Arithmetic. A classic introduction to finite fields, $p$-adic fields, quadratic forms, the Hasse–Minkowski theorem, Dirichlet $L$-series, and modular forms for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$.

title: Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology
note: Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology. Bott and Tu's book about de Rham cohomology, Mayer–Vietoris sequences, Poincaré duality, the Thom isomorphism, and spectral sequences.

title: Galois Representations of Elliptic Curves
note: Galois Representations of Elliptic Curves. English translation of Serre's 1972 paper on the open image theorem for $\ell$-adic representations $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}) \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)$ of non-CM elliptic curves.

title: Lectures on N(X)
note: Lectures on N(X). Serre's lectures on how to count rational points on algebraic varieties over finite fields. They also include exponential sums and Chebyshev-type bounds.

title: The Six-Functor Formalism on Infinity-Categories
note: The Six-Functor Formalism on Infinity-Categories. Scholze's paper gives the six-functor formalism as a lax symmetric monoidal functor from a category of correspondences $\operatorname{Corr}(\mathcal{C}, E)$ to $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. It gives the formulation of pushforward $f_*$, proper pushforward $f_!$, pullback $f^*$, exceptional pullback $f^!$, tensor product $\otimes$, and internal $\operatorname{\mathcal{R}Hom}$. It deduces proper base change and the projection formula $f_!(A \otimes f^*B) \cong f_!(A) \otimes B$. For this, it uses Lurie's straightening/unstraightening for Cartesian fibrations over $\operatorname{Fin}_*$. It also discusses cohomological smoothness, local Verdier duality, and base change for rigid-analytic and perfectoid spaces.

title: De Rham Cohomology on the Fargues-Fontaine Curve
note: De Rham Cohomology on the Fargues-Fontaine Curve. It examines the de Rham period map and vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve in $p$-adic Hodge theory.

title: Interview with Alain Connes
note: Interview with Alain Connes. His views on noncommutative geometry, quantum mechanics, and the philosophy of mathematical research.

title: Connes EMS Interview
note: Connes EMS Interview. Discussion of noncommutative geometry, the Riemann hypothesis, the Triangle of Thoughts, and the culture of contemporary mathematics.

title: Connes on Mathematical Discovery
note: Connes on Mathematical Discovery. Alain Connes tells why it is important to base concepts on computation. He also tells why it is important to examine non-invariant structures and to organize mathematical ideas conceptually.

title: Independent Problem Solving
note: Independent Problem Solving. Alain Connes on the independent study of mathematics, on deep reflection, and on challenges to the existing mathematical dogma.

title: Plant Analogies and Mental Imagery
note: Plant Analogies and Mental Imagery. Interview on Kiyoshi Oka's transplantation metaphor for mathematical analogies. It also discusses the role of mental imagery in noncommutative geometry.

title: Quadratic Forms in Homotopy Theory
note: Quadratic Forms in Homotopy Theory. Hopkins and Singer on quadratic functions in differential cohomology, refined invariants, and generalized differential characters.

title: Universal Homotopy Theories
note: Universal Homotopy Theories. Dugger's paper makes universal model categories from simplicial presheaves on small categories through homotopy colimits.

title: Differential Cohomology as Sheaves of Spectra
note: Differential Cohomology as Sheaves of Spectra. Bunke, Nikolaus, and Völkl's formulation of differential generalized cohomology theories as sheaves of spectra over the site of smooth manifolds.

title: Cohomology Operations in Differential Cohomology
note: Cohomology Operations in Differential Cohomology. Grady and Sati on primary and secondary cohomology operations in differential cohomology through higher stacks.

title: Differential Cohomology via Stacks
note: Differential Cohomology via Stacks. A geometric description of differential cohomology theories, higher gauge fields, and primary operations. It uses smooth $\infty$-stacks.

title: Introduction to Differential Cohomology
note: Introduction to Differential Cohomology. Arun Debray's 20-page primer on differential cohomology $\widehat{H}^k(M; \mathbb{Z})$, Cheeger–Simons differential characters, characteristic classes, Chern–Weil theory, and connections on line bundles. It also gives physical applications to gauge theory.

title: Cohomology and Congruences
note: Cohomology and Congruences. Slides on modular congruences, Galois representations, and calculations in group cohomology.

title: Persistence and Steenrod Operations
note: Persistence and Steenrod Operations. Applications of the Steenrod algebra and stable cohomology operations to persistent homology in topological data analysis.

title: Torsors
note: Torsors, Topoi, and Sheaf Cohomology. Introduction to global elements, $G$-torsors, and classifying topoi. It classifies $H^1(X, G)$ as isomorphism classes of $G$-torsors, and $H^2$ as sheaves of groupoids/gerbes. It also gives connections to homotopy type theory.

title: Fukaya Categories: Lecture 1
note: Fukaya Categories: Lecture 1. Introduction to symplectic manifolds, Lagrangian submanifolds, and intersection theory in Floer homology.

title: Fukaya Categories: Lecture 2
note: Fukaya Categories: Lecture 2. Moduli spaces of pseudo-holomorphic discs, Gromov compactness, and the definition of Floer cohomology.

title: Fukaya Categories: Lecture 3
note: Fukaya Categories: Lecture 3. The construction of the $A_\infty$-algebra structure on Lagrangian Floer complexes, and the higher composition operations $m_k$.

title: Homological Mirror Symmetry Course
note: Homological Mirror Symmetry Course. Introduction to Kontsevich's Homological Mirror Symmetry conjecture, which relates $D^b \operatorname{Coh}(X)$ and the Fukaya category $\operatorname{Fuk}(X^\vee)$.

title: Introduction to A-Infinity Algebras
note: Introduction to A-Infinity Algebras. Bernhard Keller's 30-page introduction to $A_\infty$-algebras, $A_\infty$-categories, modules, and their derived categories.

title: Symmetry-Protected Topological Phases
note: Symmetry-Protected Topological Phases. Generalized cohomology theories, cobordism classifications, and topological phases of matter.

title: Gerbes and Electromagnetic Duality
note: Gerbes and Electromagnetic Duality. A formulation of abelian gauge theory and electric-magnetic duality with bundle gerbes and Deligne cohomology.

title: Cohomological Support Varieties
note: Cohomological Support Varieties. Julia Pevtsova's slides on support varieties, rank varieties, and modular representation theory of finite groups.

title: Notes on Group Cohomology
note: Notes on Group Cohomology. 38-page lecture notes about group rings $\mathbb{Z}[G]$, projective resolutions, chain complexes, derived functors $\operatorname{Ext}_{\mathbb{Z}[G]}^*(\mathbb{Z}, M)$, and low-degree cohomology.

title: The Steenrod Algebra and Hopf Algebras
note: The Steenrod Algebra and Hopf Algebras. Stable cohomology operations, the Steenrod squares $\text{Sq}^k$, and the dual Steenrod algebra as a Hopf algebra.

title: Computations in the Steenrod Algebra
note: Computations in the Steenrod Algebra. A 14-page presentation that gives the details of the Adem relations, the Milnor basis, and the Cartan formula.

title: Non-Technical Introduction to the Steenrod Algebra
note: Non-Technical Introduction to the Steenrod Algebra. A conceptual explanation of the total Steenrod operation as a perturbation of the Frobenius map in topology.

title: Operators on the Bloch Space
note: Operators on the Bloch Space. Boundedness and isometries of multiplication and composition operators on Hardy spaces $H^p$ and the Bloch space $\mathcal{B}$ of the open unit disk.

title: Introduction to Operator Theory I
note: Introduction to Operator Theory I. Survey of Banach spaces, Hilbert spaces, bounded linear operators, and adjoints.

title: Introduction to Operator Theory II
note: Introduction to Operator Theory II. Spectral theory of linear operators, point spectrum, continuous spectrum, and resolvent operators.

title: Oriented Cobordism Ring
note: Oriented Cobordism Ring. Ranicki's slides on cobordism classes of closed oriented $m$-manifolds, disjoint unions, and the oriented cobordism ring $\Omega_*^{\text{SO}}$.

title: Differential Cohomology and Geometric Quantization
note: Differential Cohomology and Geometric Quantization. It refines generalized cohomology with smooth differential forms, to capture gauge holonomies and Chern–Simons invariants. It includes $H^2(X, \mathbb{Z})$ as isomorphism classes of Hermitian line bundles with $U(1)$-connections. It also includes Dirac charge quantization, Cheeger–Simons differential characters, and secondary intersection pairings.

title: Differential Cohomology via Sheaves of Spectra
note: Differential Cohomology via Sheaves of Spectra. A complete survey. It gives the definition of differential cohomology theories as objects in the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{Shv}(\operatorname{Mfld}, \operatorname{Sp})$ of sheaves of spectra on smooth manifolds. It includes derived categories $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z})$ and recollement theory.

title: Short Overview of Differential Cohomology
note: Short Overview of Differential Cohomology. Peter Haine's 7-page notes on the axiomatic definition and geometric models of differential cohomology.

title: Comprehensive Differential Cohomology
note: Comprehensive Differential Cohomology. Arun Debray's 200+ page monograph on Simons–Sullivan differential characters, generalized differential cohomology, and topological field theories.

title: Lectures on the de Rham Complex
note: Lectures on the de Rham Complex. Luc Illusie's 66 slides on algebraic de Rham cohomology, the de Rham–Witt complex, and crystalline cohomology.

title: Foundations of Six-Functor Formalisms
note: Foundations of Six-Functor Formalisms. Martin Gallauer's monograph tells about the categorical framework of the six functors ($f^*, f_*, f_!, f^!, \otimes, \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}$) on coefficient systems. It gives the formulation of Grothendieck duality, relative purity, proper and smooth base change, localization exact triangles, and $\mathbb{A}^1$-homotopy invariance. It discusses constructible $\ell$-adic sheaves and holonomic $\mathcal{D}$-modules. It also discusses the categorical representation of homology and cohomology through the tensor unit $\mathbf{1}$.

title: Fourier-Mukai Transforms and Push-Pull Duality
note: Fourier-Mukai Transforms and Push-Pull Duality. Derived push-pull integral transforms $\Phi_{\mathcal{P}}(\mathcal{F}) = \mathbf{R}q_*(\mathcal{P} \otimes^{\mathbf{L}} p^*\mathcal{F})$ between derived categories of coherent sheaves and their extensions to $T^n$-principal bundles.

title: Integral Transforms for Coherent Sheaves
note: Integral Transforms for Coherent Sheaves. David Nadler's paper on integral transforms, categorical convolution, and geometric representation theory.

title: Integral Transforms and Drinfeld Centers
note: Integral Transforms and Drinfeld Centers. Ben-Zvi, Francis, and Nadler on integral transforms for categorical sheaves and the character theory of Drinfeld centers.

title: Equivariant Homotopy and Cohomology
note: Equivariant Homotopy and Cohomology. 68-page lecture notes by Bert Guillou on $G$-spaces, equivariant homotopy groups, Bredon cohomology, and equivariant spectra.

title: Introduction to q-de Rham Cohomology
note: Introduction to q-de Rham Cohomology. Ferdinand Wagner's exposition of $q$-de Rham cohomology, $q$-connections, and Habiro rings.

title: Sheaves on Manifolds and Efimov K-Theory
note: Sheaves on Manifolds and Efimov K-Theory. Nikolaus's paper makes six-functor formalisms on $\operatorname{Shv}(X; \mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}))$ for locally compact Hausdorff spaces. For this, it uses compactly assembled presentable stable $\infty$-categories and Efimov's continuous $K$-theory. It gives the details of dualizable categories, rigid monoidal categories, Frobenius algebras, and the self-duality of $\operatorname{Shv}(X; \operatorname{Sp})$.

title: Algebraic Surgery over the Integers
note: Algebraic Surgery over the Integers. Lecture notes on algebraic surgery theory and Gromov–Witten invariants over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}$.

title: Frobenius Homomorphisms in Higher Algebra
note: Frobenius Homomorphisms in Higher Algebra. Thomas Nikolaus's ICM slides on topological Hochschild homology (THH), topological cyclic homology (TC), and cyclotomic spectra.

title: Algebraic Geometry I-III
note: Algebraic Geometry I-III. Nikolaus's lecture notes about schemes, sheaves, cohomology, and moduli theory.

title: Gestalten and Stefanich Rings
note: Gestalten and Stefanich Rings. Scholze's 90-page paper on Gestalten and the geometry of Stefanich rings. It gives higher Tannakian duality for symmetric monoidal presentable categories $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$, $\kappa$-compactly generated categories, and affine stacks. It examines $n$-affineness, non-flat descent, and categorified analytic geometry in $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Pr}_{\text{st}}^L)$.

title: Lectures on Banach Spaces
note: Lectures on Banach Spaces. Lecture notes on functional analysis, dual spaces, weak topologies, and spectral theory.

title: Origins of Sheaf Theory
note: Origins of Sheaf Theory. A historical account of how Leray, Cartan, Serre, and Grothendieck made the theory of sheaves.

title: AMS What Is
note: AMS What Is...? Column Collection. Expository articles about foundational mathematical concepts.

title: Sobolev Sheaves and Subanalytic Sites
note: Sobolev Sheaves and Subanalytic Sites. Luca Prelli's 99 slides about sheaf theory on subanalytic and o-minimal sites. They include the DTOP site, tempered holomorphic functions, ultrafilter compactifications, the spectral topology on fibres, and the six-functor formalism for subanalytic sheaves.

title: Concise Introduction to Almost Ring Theory
note: Concise Introduction to Almost Ring Theory. Bhargav Bhatt's notes on Faltings' almost mathematics over a perfectoid field $K$. They examine the valuation ring $K^\circ$ with idempotent maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m} = \mathfrak{m}^2$. Localization at the Serre subcategory $\Sigma$ of $\mathfrak{m}$-torsion modules gives the category of almost modules $K^{\circ a}\text{-}\mathbf{Mod} = K^\circ\text{-}\mathbf{Mod} / \Sigma$. The notes include almost flatness, almost projective modules, diagonal idempotents, almost étale morphisms, and deformation theory through the almost purity theorem.

title: L-Functions and Partition Functions
note: L-Functions and Partition Functions. A thesis that examines the connections between partition functions, modular forms, and thermodynamics.

title: Introduction to L-Functions
note: Introduction to L-Functions. PV's slides about Dirichlet series $D_f(s) = \sum f(n)n^{-s}$, Dirichlet characters, conductors, local Euler factors, completed $L$-functions, and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis.

title: Dedekind Zeta Functions and Number Fields
note: Dedekind Zeta Functions and Number Fields. It includes the Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K(s) = \sum_{\mathfrak{a}} N(\mathfrak{a})^{-s}$, the analytic class number formula, Dirichlet's unit theorem, decomposition groups $D_{\mathfrak{p}}$, inertia groups $I_{\mathfrak{p}}$, and Frobenius automorphisms.

title: Tutorial on the Riemann Zeta Function
note: Tutorial on the Riemann Zeta Function. Michel Waldschmidt's complete 192-page tutorial on the analytic properties, special values, and zeros of $\zeta(s)$.

title: Artin and Hasse-Weil L-Functions
note: Artin and Hasse-Weil L-Functions. Slides on Artin $L$-functions attached to Galois representations, Artin's conjecture, and local Euler factors of algebraic varieties.

title: The Selberg Class and Langlands Philosophy
note: The Selberg Class and Langlands Philosophy. Overview of the Selberg class of $L$-functions, functional equations, automorphic representations, and the Langlands correspondence.

title: Pierre Samuel's Algebraic Theory of Numbers
note: Pierre Samuel's Algebraic Theory of Numbers. Text on Dedekind domains, ideal class groups, prime ideal factorizations, and the geometry of numbers.

title: An L-Function Approach to Class Field Theory
note: An L-Function Approach to Class Field Theory. A 101-page monograph. It gives the formulation of global and local class field theory through the analytic properties and factorization of abelian $L$-functions.

title: Notes on Almost Mathematics
note: Notes on Almost Mathematics. Peter Scholze's condensed notes on almost ring theory, almost étale algebras, and their role in the foundations of perfectoid geometry.

title: Notes on t-Structures and Constructibility
note: Notes on t-Structures and Constructibility. Ofer Gabber's notes on constructible sheaves, perverse sheaves, and $t$-structures on derived categories over schemes.

title: Grothendieck-Verdier Duality and Autonomous Categories
note: Grothendieck-Verdier Duality and Autonomous Categories. Boyarchenko and Drinfeld on *-autonomous categories, Grothendieck–Verdier categories, and dualizing objects in constructible derived categories.

title: Representability of Derived Stacks
note: Representability of Derived Stacks. J.P. Pridham's criteria for the representability of derived Artin stacks and formal moduli problems. The criteria use deformation theory and simplicial rings.

title: Numerical Linear Algebra Tutorial
note: Numerical Linear Algebra Tutorial. 235 slides that review vector spaces, matrix factorizations (LU, QR, SVD), and iterative linear solvers.

title: Applied Linear Algebra by Stephen Boyd
note: Applied Linear Algebra by Stephen Boyd. Slides about vectors, matrices, least squares, QR factorization, and symmetric eigenvalue decompositions.

title: Random Matrix Theory and Free Probability
note: Random Matrix Theory and Free Probability. Benoît Collins's 79 slides. They give a survey of Gaussian ensembles, Haar unitary matrices, and free probability.

title: Linear Algebra Course Slides
note: Linear Algebra Course Slides. 501 slides about systems of linear equations, eigenspaces, orthogonality, and the spectral theorem.

title: Random Matrix Theory for Machine Learning
note: Random Matrix Theory for Machine Learning. ICML tutorial on the spectral properties of high-dimensional random matrices, and on spectral clustering.

title: Derived Induction and Restriction
note: Derived Induction and Restriction. Matthew Ando and Justin Noel on derived induction, equivariant cohomology, and transfer maps in chromatic homotopy theory.

title: Derived Induction in Equivariant Homotopy
note: Derived Induction in Equivariant Homotopy. Justin Noel's slides on derived induction theorems and transfer arguments for equivariant ring spectra.

title: The Transfer Argument in Stable Homotopy
note: The Transfer Argument in Stable Homotopy. Slides on Artin–Tate motives, the transfer map, and Adams–Novikov spectral sequences.

title: L-Functions and Random Matrix Theory
note: L-Functions and Random Matrix Theory. Brian Conrey's talk on the distribution of zeros of $L$-functions and eigenvalue statistics of the Circular Unitary Ensemble (CUE).

title: Anderson Duality for Derived Stacks
note: Anderson Duality for Derived Stacks. Sanath Devalapurkar's notes on Anderson duality, topological modular forms ($\operatorname{tmf}$), and the Brown–Comenetz dual of ring spectra.

title: Random Matrix Theory Foundations
note: Random Matrix Theory Foundations. Zhenyu Liao's lecture series on Marchenko–Pastur distributions, resolvent methods, and concentration.

title: Matrix Computations Course
note: Matrix Computations Course. The course homepage. The course includes matrix decompositions, Rayleigh quotients, and convex optimization.

title: Matrix Computation Slides
note: Matrix Computation Slides. Lecture slides on advanced numerical linear algebra, low-rank approximations, and spectral graph theory.

title: Almost Ring Theory
note: Almost Ring Theory. Gabber and Ramero's foundational treatise of more than 300 pages. It is about almost ring theory, non-flat descent, cotangent complexes, and $p$-adic Hodge theory.

title: Topology in Quantum Field Theory
note: Topology in Quantum Field Theory. Dan Freed's CBMS lectures on topological quantum field theories, bordism categories, and characteristic classes.

title: Anderson Duality in Stable Homotopy Theory
note: Anderson Duality in Stable Homotopy Theory. Stojanoska's paper calculates Anderson duality for the spectrum of topological modular forms $\operatorname{tmf}[1/2]$ as a 21-fold suspension. It connects formal groups, Morava $K$-theories, and Deligne–Mumford moduli stacks of elliptic curves.

title: Star-Autonomous Categories and the Chu Construction
note: Star-Autonomous Categories and the Chu Construction. Michael Barr's paper on how to make *-autonomous categories with the Chu construction over cartesian closed categories.

title: History of the Chu Construction
note: History of the Chu Construction. Barr's survey on the origin of *-autonomous categories, linear logic, and duality in computer science and category theory.

title: Representability Theorems in Derived Geometry
note: Representability Theorems in Derived Geometry. Jacob Lurie's DAG XIV. It gives representability criteria for derived Artin stacks and dualizing modules.

title: Introduction to Algebraic Stacks
note: Introduction to Algebraic Stacks. Adeel Khan's notes on simplicial sets, Kan horn filling conditions, $\infty$-categories, sheaves, stacks, and descent through totalization.

title: Additive Combinatorics
note: Additive Combinatorics. Terence Tao and Van Vu's monograph on sumset estimates, Freiman's theorem, Szemerédi's regularity lemma, and the polynomial method.

title: Probability and Geometry on Groups
note: Probability and Geometry on Groups. Gábor Pete's book on random walks on groups, percolation, expander graphs, and geometric group theory.

title: Compact Closed Categories in Homotopical Algebra
note: Compact Closed Categories in Homotopical Algebra. Survey of compact closed and *-autonomous categories, dualizable objects, and their classification in homotopical algebra.

title: Distribution of Class Groups
note: Distribution of Class Groups. Landesman's notes on the Cohen–Lenstra heuristics, Minkowski bounds, $\Gamma$-Hurwitz spaces, and the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula over $\mathbb{F}_q(t)$.

title: Algebraic Combinatorics and Symmetric Functions
note: Algebraic Combinatorics and Symmetric Functions. Slides about Schur functions, Young tableaux, the Littlewood–Richardson rule, Schubert calculus, and 3-point Gromov–Witten invariants.

title: Lectures on Condensed Mathematics
note: Lectures on Condensed Mathematics. Peter Scholze's notes that give the foundations of condensed sets, condensed abelian groups, solid abelian groups, and analytic rings. They prove generation by compact projectives through Stone–Čech compactifications of profinite sets.

title: Guidelines for the Six-Functor Formalism
note: Guidelines for the Six-Functor Formalism. Caleb Ji's summary of Scholze's 6-functor formalism on stable $\infty$-categories of sheaves, base change, projection formulas, and Verdier duality.

title: Six-Functor Formalism for Motives
note: Six-Functor Formalism for Motives. Joseph Ayoub's treatise on the six-functor formalism in motivic homotopy theory and cross-functors.

title: Six Functors for Analytic Stacks
note: Six Functors for Analytic Stacks. Dauser's 13-page summary of the six-functor formalism for $p$-adic analytic stacks.

title: Verdier Duality in Topology
note: Verdier Duality in Topology. 20-page expository notes on Verdier duality, compact support pushforward $f_!$, and exceptional pullback $f^!$.

title: Foundations of Condensed Mathematics
note: Foundations of Condensed Mathematics. Dagur Asgeirsson's 100-page master's thesis. It gives an accessible introduction to condensed sets, solid modules, and liquid vector spaces.

title: Uniqueness of Six-Functor Formalisms
note: Uniqueness of Six-Functor Formalisms. It shows the axiomatic uniqueness and rigidity of the six-functor formalism on geometric categories.

title: Homological Algebra and Sheaves
note: Homological Algebra and Sheaves. Jean Gallier's complete 600-page treatise on homological algebra, sheaf cohomology, and spectral sequences.

title: Lusztig Induction and Restriction
note: Lusztig Induction and Restriction. Gérard Laumon's slides on character sheaves, Deligne–Lusztig induction, and representations of finite reductive groups.

title: Logarithmic Geometry and Desingularization
note: Logarithmic Geometry and Desingularization. Michael Temkin's slides on logarithmic geometry, canonical resolution of singularities, and functorial desingularization.

title: Étale Cohomology Notes
note: Étale Cohomology Notes. 93-page complete course notes about étale sites, proper base change, and the Weil conjectures.

title: Lubin-Tate Theory Notes
note: Lubin-Tate Theory Notes. 141-page lecture notes on formal groups, Lubin–Tate deformation spaces, and local class field theory.

title: Arithmetic Langlands Notes
note: Arithmetic Langlands Notes. 103-page course notes on automorphic forms, Galois representations, and the arithmetic Langlands correspondence.

title: The Fargues-Fontaine Curve
note: The Fargues-Fontaine Curve. 85-page lecture notes on the schematic and adic Fargues–Fontaine curve in $p$-adic Hodge theory.

title: Solid Group Cohomology
note: Solid Group Cohomology. 18-page notes on the condensation functor on topological groups and solid cohomology for locally profinite groups.

title: Algebraic Geometry I Notes
note: Algebraic Geometry I Notes. Peter Scholze's course notes on affine schemes, projective schemes, sheaves, and scheme-theoretic constructions.

title: Algebraic Geometry II: Sheaf Cohomology
note: Algebraic Geometry II: Sheaf Cohomology. Scholze's notes about flat and smooth morphisms, Hilbert polynomials, Serre duality, and the Riemann–Roch theorem for curves.

title: Chromatic Homotopy Theory I
note: Chromatic Homotopy Theory I. Agnès Beaudry's introduction to complex cobordism $\operatorname{MU}$, formal group laws, and the Adams–Novikov spectral sequence.

title: Chromatic Homotopy Theory II
note: Chromatic Homotopy Theory II. Morava $K$-theories $K(n)$, Morava $E$-theories $E_n$, and the chromatic filtration.

title: Chromatic Homotopy Theory III
note: Chromatic Homotopy Theory III. The chromatic spectral sequence, chromatic convergence, and the telescope conjecture.

title: Formal Geometric Series in Projective Geometry
note: Formal Geometric Series in Projective Geometry. Littlewood-style heuristic expansions, such as $\frac{\mathbb{C}^{n+1} \setminus \{0\}}{\mathbb{C} \setminus \{0\}} = \mathbb{C}^n + \dots + \mathbb{C}^1 + 1$. Such an expansion shows the cell decomposition of $\mathbb{P}^n$.

title: Painless Conjugate Gradient Method
note: Painless Conjugate Gradient Method. Jonathan Shewchuk's classic guide to the conjugate gradient method and to the optimization of positive-definite quadratic forms.

title: Local Monodromy and Compatible Systems
note: Local Monodromy and Compatible Systems. Weizhe Zheng's slides on local monodromy, $\ell$-adic representations, and compatible systems of Galois representations.

title: Sheaves
note: Sheaves, Germs, and Constant Sheaves. Misha Verbitsky's notes on stalks, germs, direct limits of section modules, and the characterization of constant sheaves.

title: Vanishing and Nearby Cycles
note: Vanishing and Nearby Cycles. 54 slides on vanishing cycles $R\Psi$ and $R\Phi$, local systems on punctured discs, and Milnor fibers over general bases.

title: Mod-l Cohomology Algebras
note: Mod-l Cohomology Algebras. Slides on mod-$\ell$ étale cohomology algebras, cycle classes, and cup product structures.

title: Mod-l Equivariant Cohomology
note: Mod-l Equivariant Cohomology. 43 slides on Cartesian sheaves, equivariant étale cohomology, and Grothendieck topologies.

title: Prismatic F-Gauges
note: Prismatic F-Gauges. Bhargav Bhatt's lecture notes on prismatic $F$-gauges, Breuil–Kisin twists, syntomic cohomology, Nygaard filtrations, and topological cyclic homology.

title: John Baez on Motives
note: John Baez on Motives. Expository notes that tell about Grothendieck's motives, Weil cohomology theories, and how to count points on projective spaces.

title: Berkovich Motives
note: Berkovich Motives. Peter Scholze's paper on Berkovich spectra, arc sheaves, the arc topology, and the derived category of Berkovich motives $\mathcal{D}_{\text{mot}}(X)$.

title: Wild Betti Sheaves
note: Wild Betti Sheaves. Scholze's paper gives the theory of wild Betti sheaves through Verdier quotients, exponential local systems, and the Fourier transform on ring stacks.

title: Zagier on the Dilogarithm
note: Zagier on the Dilogarithm. Don Zagier's survey on the dilogarithm $\operatorname{Li}_2(z)$, the Bloch–Wigner function $D(z)$, hyperbolic 3-manifold volumes, and the Bloch group $B(F)$.

title: Meromorphic Continuation of Eisenstein Series
note: Meromorphic Continuation of Eisenstein Series. A proof of the meromorphic continuation of adelic Eisenstein series. The proof uses convolution algebras of compactly supported smooth functions and Cramer's rule.

title: O-Minimal Geometry and Hyperbolic Manifolds
note: O-Minimal Geometry and Hyperbolic Manifolds. Applications of o-minimal structures, semialgebraic sets, and tame topology to cusp shapes and hyperbolic Dehn fillings.

title: Survey on Dehn Surgery
note: Survey on Dehn Surgery. Survey of Dehn surgery, prime 3-manifold decompositions, and hyperbolic knot complements.

title: Surgery on Compact Manifolds
note: Surgery on Compact Manifolds. Wall's foundational book on surgery theory, $L$-groups, and the classification of high-dimensional manifolds.

title: Affine Homology of Stacks
note: Affine Homology of Stacks. The definition and calculation of the affine homology of affine stacks. It also gives base change theorems and dimensional filtrations.

title: K-Theory of Moduli Stacks
note: K-Theory of Moduli Stacks. Explicit calculations of pushforwards, hyperplane classes, self-intersection formulas, and the localization theorem in the $K$-theory of moduli strata.

title: Stacks and Perfect Complexes
note: Stacks and Perfect Complexes. It examines higher Artin 2-stacks, automorphism groupoids $\mathbb{G}_m \times \mathbb{G}_m \times B\mathbb{G}_a$, and descent conditions for perfect complexes.

title: The Resolution Property for Stacks
note: The Resolution Property for Stacks. Burt Totaro's paper gives a characterization of the algebraic stacks that admit resolutions of coherent sheaves by vector bundles.

title: The Tenfold Way and Superalgebras
note: The Tenfold Way and Superalgebras. John Baez on real division algebras ($\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}$), super vector spaces, Clifford algebras, and Dyson's tenfold classification of topological matter.

title: Spin Groups and Clifford Superalgebras
note: Spin Groups and Clifford Superalgebras. Deligne's notes on quadratic vector spaces, Spin groups, spinor representations, Bott periodicity modulo 8, and the super Brauer group.

title: Grothendieck-Teichmuller Theory and Dessins d'Enfants
note: Grothendieck-Teichmuller Theory and Dessins d'Enfants. Survey on Grothendieck's dessins d'enfants, bipartite ribbon graphs, the absolute Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$, and the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group $\widehat{GT}$.

title: Drinfeld Associators and Braided Categories
note: Drinfeld Associators and Braided Categories. A universal construction of braided monoidal categories from Lie algebras, quasi-Hopf algebras, and solutions to the Kashiwara–Vergne conjecture.

title: Conceptual Proof of the Sylow Theorems
note: Conceptual Proof of the Sylow Theorems. Qiaochu Yuan's exposition. It uses $p$-group actions on finite sets, orbit-stabilizer relations, and fixed-point congruences $|X^G| \equiv |X| \pmod p$.

title: Hodge Correlators and Motivic Periods
note: Hodge Correlators and Motivic Periods. Alexander Goncharov on Hodge correlators, dilogarithms, the Bloch–Wigner function, and twistor interpretations of Archimedean periods.

title: Motivic Fundamental Groups of CM Elliptic Curves
note: Motivic Fundamental Groups of CM Elliptic Curves. Applications of higher-weight Hodge correlators to the motivic fundamental groups of elliptic curves with complex multiplication.

title: Hodge Correlators by Goncharov
note: Hodge Correlators by Goncharov. Foundational paper on Hodge correlators, Feynman integrals on Riemann surfaces, and mixed Hodge structures on fundamental groups.

title: Higher Fukaya Categories and Shifted Symplectic Stacks
note: Higher Fukaya Categories and Shifted Symplectic Stacks. A speculative framework for higher Fukaya categories $n\operatorname{Fuk}(X)$. These categories are associated with $(n-1)$-shifted symplectic stacks and iterated derived intersections.

title: Geometric Langlands Course Notes
note: Geometric Langlands Course Notes. Arun Debray's notes about the spectral dictionary, continuous and discrete spectra of commuting operators, and the geometric Langlands correspondence.

title: Introduction to Fukaya Categories
note: Introduction to Fukaya Categories. Denis Auroux's lecture notes on pseudo-holomorphic strips, Lagrangian Floer cohomology, transversality, and $A_\infty$-operations.

title: Zeta Spectral Triples
note: Zeta Spectral Triples. Alain Connes on spectral zeta functions, regularized determinants, and non-commutative geometry of the Riemann zeros.

title: Duality and Linearization for p-Adic Lie Groups
note: Duality and Linearization for p-Adic Lie Groups. Dustin Clausen's thesis on Lazard–Poincaré duality for compact $p$-adic Lie groups, tangent deformations, and the six-functor formalism on $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Q}_p^\times$.

title: Geometric and Arithmetic Theta Correspondences
note: Geometric and Arithmetic Theta Correspondences. Chao Li's IHES lectures on the Kudla program, unitary group cycles, and arithmetic intersection theory.

title: Introduction to Shimura Varieties
note: Introduction to Shimura Varieties. 17-slide overview of Shimura data, hermitian symmetric domains, and arithmetic quotients.

title: Sophie Morel on Shimura Varieties
note: Sophie Morel on Shimura Varieties. 65-page survey on the cohomology of Shimura varieties, weighted truncation, and intersection cohomology.

title: Twisted Automorphic Descent and GGP
note: Twisted Automorphic Descent and GGP. Chao Li and Lei Zhang's slides on the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture and automorphic descent for classical groups.

title: Perfectoid Siegel Spaces
note: Perfectoid Siegel Spaces. Peter Scholze's paper gives Galois representations associated with the mod-$p$ cohomology of locally symmetric spaces and Siegel modular varieties.

title: Guide to the Six-Functor Formalism
note: Guide to the Six-Functor Formalism. Lucas Mann's complete 196-page guide to the six-functor formalism on correspondences, Cartesian fibrations, and étale/rigid categories.

title: Six Functors in Rigid Analytic Geometry
note: Six Functors in Rigid Analytic Geometry. Lucas Mann's monograph gives the 6-functor formalism for $p$-torsion étale sheaves on rigid-analytic and perfectoid spaces.

title: Matroids and Simplicial Complexes
note: Matroids and Simplicial Complexes. Pure simplicial complexes, uniform matroids, graphic matroids, and independent sets.

title: Binary Geometry of Generalized Permutohedra
note: Binary Geometry of Generalized Permutohedra. Associadedra, permutohedra, and scattering amplitude geometry in mathematical physics.

title: Tropical Geometry and Mirror Symmetry
note: Tropical Geometry and Mirror Symmetry. Hiroshi Iritani's slides on period asymptotics, tropical disks, and mirror symmetry.

title: Introduction to Shimura Varieties by Kai-Wen Lan
note: Introduction to Shimura Varieties by Kai-Wen Lan. Basic examples of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$, Shimura data $(G, X)$, and moduli spaces of abelian varieties with PEL structures.

title: Stacky Approach to p-Adic Hodge Theory
note: Stacky Approach to p-Adic Hodge Theory. Formal stacks, de Rham complexes, and Hodge filtrations for group schemes such as $\mathbb{G}_a$.

title: Milne's Introduction to Shimura Varieties
note: Milne's Introduction to Shimura Varieties. Notes that give the foundations of bounded symmetric domains, Siegel modular varieties, and canonical models.

title: Convex Polytopes and Braid Cones
note: Convex Polytopes and Braid Cones. Combinatorial dictionary between preposets, braid arrangements, and normal fans of permutohedra.

title: Kronecker's First Limit Formula
note: Kronecker's First Limit Formula. A derivation and calculations for binary quadratic forms and the Dedekind eta function.

title: Habiro Cohomology and Quantum Invariants
note: Habiro Cohomology and Quantum Invariants. Ferdinand Wagner's PhD thesis on $q$-de Rham cohomology, Habiro rings, hyperbolic knot volumes, and dilogarithms.

title: Arithmetic Topology and Gauge Theory
note: Arithmetic Topology and Gauge Theory. Minhyong Kim's slides on the arithmetic dictionary between 3-manifolds and number rings, arithmetic Chern–Simons theory, and path integrals.

title: Arithmetic Topology and Modular Curves
note: Arithmetic Topology and Modular Curves. Don Zagier's Hirzebruch Lecture. It examines differential equations, Legendre elliptic curves, and topology.

title: Notes on Lambda-Rings
note: Notes on Lambda-Rings. Darij Grinberg's introduction to $\lambda$-rings, Adams operations, representation rings, and symmetric functions.

title: History of Polylogarithms and Regulators
note: History of Polylogarithms and Regulators. Richard Hain's slides on polylogarithms, Dirichlet's unit theorem, regulators, and mapping class groups.

title: Tannakian Categories by J
note: Tannakian Categories by J.S. Milne. A complete survey of Tannakian categories, fiber functors, affine group schemes, and fundamental groups.

title: Classification of Topological Vector Bundles
note: Classification of Topological Vector Bundles. The homotopy classification of real and complex vector bundles over CW complexes through Grassmannians.

title: Borcherds Products and Automorphic Forms
note: Borcherds Products and Automorphic Forms. Henri Darmon's exposition on Borcherds products, theta lifts, and singular moduli.

title: Theory of 2-Gerbes and Picard Groupoids
note: Theory of 2-Gerbes and Picard Groupoids. A categorical definition of algebraic group scheme gerbes, band structures, and modules over Picard groupoids $\operatorname{Pic}^\mathbb{Z}$.

title: Siegel Modular Forms Introduction
note: Siegel Modular Forms Introduction. Basic theory of the Siegel upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}_g$, the symplectic group $\operatorname{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb{Z})$, and Siegel modular forms.

title: Rational Algebraic K-Theory
note: Rational Algebraic K-Theory. Calculations and structural results in the rational algebraic $K$-theory of schemes and rings.

title: Baxter Q-Operators and Quantum Integrable Systems
note: Baxter Q-Operators and Quantum Integrable Systems. Connections between Baxter $Q$-operators, quantum groups, and representations of the Weil group.

title: The Deligne-Ihara Conjecture
note: The Deligne-Ihara Conjecture. Exposition of periods, mixed Tate motives, and the action of the motivic Galois group on the fundamental group of $\mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0,1,\infty\}$.

title: Algebraic K-Theory of Finite Fields
note: Algebraic K-Theory of Finite Fields. Peter Haine's notes on Quillen's calculation of $K_*(\mathbb{F}_q)$ through the plus construction $B\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb{F}_q)^+$ and the Adams conjecture.

title: Classification of Topological Insulators
note: Classification of Topological Insulators. Topological states of matter, symmetry classes, and the classification through real and complex topological $K$-theory.

title: Topological K-Theory and Condensed Matter
note: Topological K-Theory and Condensed Matter. Dan Freed's lectures on twistings, the tenfold way, and the K-theory classification of topological insulators and superconductors.

title: Lefschetz Pencils and Symplectic 4-Manifolds
note: Lefschetz Pencils and Symplectic 4-Manifolds. Denis Auroux's slides on Lefschetz fibrations, monodromy representations, mapping class groups, and Hurwitz equivalence.

title: Introduction to Gromov-Witten Theory
note: Introduction to Gromov-Witten Theory. Hulya Arguz's slides on moduli of stable maps, Kontsevich's recursive formulas, virtual fundamental classes, and torus localization.

title: Relative Gromov-Witten Theory
note: Relative Gromov-Witten Theory. Nodal curve insertions, degeneration formulas, and Gromov–Witten invariants of pairs.

title: Étale Cohomology of Rigid Analytic Spaces
note: Étale Cohomology of Rigid Analytic Spaces. David Hansen's handout on the history and the modern developments of étale cohomology for adic and perfectoid spaces.

title: Simplicial Sets and Stable Homotopy Theory
note: Simplicial Sets and Stable Homotopy Theory. Slides that introduce simplicial sets, geometric realizations, spectra, and stable model categories.

title: Summary of Six-Functor Formalisms
note: Summary of Six-Functor Formalisms. Arun Soor's 23 slides. They give the definition of the six-functor formalism as a lax symmetric monoidal functor on correspondences $\operatorname{Corr}(\mathcal{C}, E) \to \operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. They include proper base change, projection formulas, and Verdier duality.

title: Poincaré Duality in Six-Functor Formalisms
note: Poincaré Duality in Six-Functor Formalisms. Formal properties of Poincaré duality, trace maps, and Verdier's diagonal trick in the six-functor context.

title: Thermodynamic Semirings and Information
note: Thermodynamic Semirings and Information. Matilde Marcolli's notes on tropical geometry, semirings, and the algebraic structure of statistical thermodynamics.

title: Class Field Theory by Jürgen Neukirch
note: Class Field Theory by Jürgen Neukirch. A complete textbook about local and global class field theory, Galois cohomology, and abstract class formations.

title: Summary of Class Field Theory
note: Summary of Class Field Theory. François Charles's concise summary of the main theorems of local and global class field theory and the Artin map.

title: Galois Cohomology and Class Field Theory
note: Galois Cohomology and Class Field Theory. 33 slides on group cohomology, Tate cohomology, Herbrand quotients, and their role in class field theory.

title: Course Notes on Class Field Theory
note: Course Notes on Class Field Theory. Sam Raskin's 119-page lecture notes about local fields, adèles, idèles, and the cohomological proofs of class field theory.

title: Galois Cohomology and Class Formations
note: Galois Cohomology and Class Formations. Hamann's notes on abstract class formations, the Tate–Nakayama theorem, and reciprocity maps.

title: Advanced Number Theory and Class Field Theory
note: Advanced Number Theory and Class Field Theory. 85-page notes about ray class groups, $L$-functions, and global reciprocity.

title: Foundations of Stable Homotopy Theory
note: Foundations of Stable Homotopy Theory. Hill, Hopkins, and Ravenel's slides on spectra, model categories, Bousfield localization, symmetric spectra, Day convolution, and smash products.

title: Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves
note: Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves. Introduction to bounded derived categories $\mathcal{D}^b(\operatorname{Coh} X)$, standard exact sequences (Euler, ideal, normal), and Fourier–Mukai transforms.

title: Physical Heuristics for Fourier-Mukai Transforms
note: Physical Heuristics for Fourier-Mukai Transforms. Discussion on Fourier–Mukai transforms as generalized T-duality. A transform maps vector bundles to skyscraper sheaves in dual abelian varieties.

title: The Nishida Nilpotence Theorem
note: The Nishida Nilpotence Theorem. Richard Wong's slides on the ring structure of stable homotopy groups of spheres $\pi_*(\mathbb{S})$ and the nilpotence of positive-degree elements.

title: Grid Homology and Floer Homotopy
note: Grid Homology and Floer Homotopy. Ciprian Manolescu's talk on grid homology, combinatorial knot Floer homology, and Floer homotopy spectra.

title: Banach Bundles and Nonarchimedean GAGA
note: Banach Bundles and Nonarchimedean GAGA. Kiran Kedlaya's 32 slides on Banach vector bundles, the Fargues–Fontaine curve, and Banach–Colmez spaces.

title: Exponential Sums and Monodromy Groups
note: Exponential Sums and Monodromy Groups. Nick Katz's lectures on $\ell$-adic local systems, geometric and arithmetic monodromy groups, and hypergeometric sheaves.

title: Applied l-Adic Cohomology
note: Applied l-Adic Cohomology. Emmanuel Kowalski's 79-page notes on trace functions, Kloosterman sums, and $\ell$-adic sheaves in analytic number theory.

title: Conductors and Complexity of Trace Functions
note: Conductors and Complexity of Trace Functions. Kowalski's slides on bounds for exponential sums, higher-dimensional trace functions, and Fourier complexity through Deligne's Weil II.

title: Simplicial Type Theory
note: Simplicial Type Theory. Formalization of Segal types, Rezk complete Segal types, and synthetic $\infty$-category theory.

title: Algebraic K-Theory of Infinite Dihedral Groups
note: Algebraic K-Theory of Infinite Dihedral Groups. Andrew Ranicki's slides on the algebraic $K$-theory, class groups, and Whitehead torsion of infinite dihedral groups.

title: Constructions in Mirror Symmetry
note: Constructions in Mirror Symmetry. Slide overview of the SYZ conjecture, mirror manifolds, and Picard–Fuchs equations.

title: Birational Geometry and Blow-Ups
note: Birational Geometry and Blow-Ups. Joaquín Moraga's slides on combinatorial projective spaces, blow-ups, flips, and the Minimal Model Program.

title: Introduction to K3 Surfaces
note: Introduction to K3 Surfaces. Adam Logan's slides on the geometry, Hodge structures, and Picard lattices of $K3$ surfaces.

title: Moduli Spaces and Homological Stability
note: Moduli Spaces and Homological Stability. Oscar Randal-Williams's slides on classifying spaces $B\operatorname{Diff}(M)$, mapping class groups $\Gamma_g$, and homological stability.

title: Positive Scalar Curvature and Index Theory
note: Positive Scalar Curvature and Index Theory. Randal-Williams's slides on the index of Dirac operators and spaces of positive scalar curvature metrics.

title: Calculus of Manifold Embeddings
note: Calculus of Manifold Embeddings. Survey on the Weiss embedding calculus, configuration spaces, and diffeomorphism groups.

title: Metastability of Mapping Class Groups
note: Metastability of Mapping Class Groups. Homological stability and high-dimensional metastabilities in mapping class groups.

title: Homological Stability in Topology
note: Homological Stability in Topology. A complete set of 35 slides on homological stability for symmetric groups, general linear groups, and moduli spaces of manifolds.

title: Scanning Operations on Manifolds
note: Scanning Operations on Manifolds. Geometric scanning methods in the cohomology of moduli spaces of surfaces.

title: Spaces of Manifolds and Fiber Bundles
note: Spaces of Manifolds and Fiber Bundles. Characteristic classes of smooth manifold bundles and Cobordism hypothesis perspectives.

title: Topology of Stable Moduli Spaces
note: Topology of Stable Moduli Spaces. The Madsen–Weiss theorem, cobordism categories, and the Mumford conjecture on the stable cohomology of $\mathcal{M}_g$.

title: Smoothing Theory of Topological Manifolds
note: Smoothing Theory of Topological Manifolds. Obstructions to smooth structures on high-dimensional topological manifolds through Kirby–Siebenmann classes.

title: Diffeomorphisms of Disks I
note: Diffeomorphisms of Disks I. It examines the homotopy types of diffeomorphism groups $\operatorname{Diff}(D^n, \partial D^n)$ and pseudoisotopies.

title: Cohomology of Moduli Spaces
note: Cohomology of Moduli Spaces. A case study about how to calculate tautological rings and the cohomology of moduli spaces of curves.

title: Tits Buildings and Diffeomorphism Groups
note: Tits Buildings and Diffeomorphism Groups. 68 slides on Tits buildings, Steinberg modules, and homological stability for arithmetic groups.

title: Diffeomorphism Groups and Cohomology
note: Diffeomorphism Groups and Cohomology. Advanced methods to examine the classifying spaces of diffeomorphism groups.

title: ICM Plenary on Diffeomorphisms of Manifolds
note: ICM Plenary on Diffeomorphisms of Manifolds. 72-page expanded survey on stable and unstable cohomology of moduli spaces of manifolds.

title: Homeomorphisms of Euclidean Space
note: Homeomorphisms of Euclidean Space. 25 slides on $\operatorname{Homeo}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, topological groups, and orthogonal calculus.

title: Miller-Morita-Mumford Classes
note: Miller-Morita-Mumford Classes. Tautological rings of moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces and generalized MMM classes.

title: Steinberg Modules and Homological Stability
note: Steinberg Modules and Homological Stability. 65 slides on duality complexes, arithmetic groups, and stability.

title: E-Infinity Algebras and General Linear Groups
note: E-Infinity Algebras and General Linear Groups. $E_\infty$-ring spectra, algebraic $K$-theory, and the Nesterenko–Suslin theorem.

title: Lecture Notes on Homotopy Theory
note: Lecture Notes on Homotopy Theory. 84-page course notes by Oscar Randal-Williams on homotopy groups, fibrations, cofibrations, and spectral sequences.

title: Introduction to Group Theory
note: Introduction to Group Theory. 75-page undergraduate course notes about group actions, Sylow theorems, and simple groups.

title: Complex Analysis in Algebraic Geometry
note: Complex Analysis in Algebraic Geometry. A 301-page treatise that connects several complex variables, Hodge theory, and complex algebraic geometry.

title: Classical Algebraic Geometry
note: Classical Algebraic Geometry. 205 slides about projective varieties, Bézout's theorem, intersection numbers, and divisors.

title: Structure of Algebraic Varieties
note: Structure of Algebraic Varieties. János Kollár's slides on the Minimal Model Program, singularities, and moduli of varieties.

title: Topological Spaces Notes
note: Topological Spaces Notes. 44-page notes on the foundations of point-set topology, compactness, connectedness, and quotient topologies.

title: Characteristic Classes and K-Theory
note: Characteristic Classes and K-Theory. 75-page lecture notes about vector bundles, Chern classes, the splitting principle, and topological $K$-theory.

title: Computations in Algebraic Geometry
note: Computations in Algebraic Geometry. 45-page notes on computational methods, Veronese embeddings, and projective coordinate rings.

title: Groups
note: Groups, Rings and Modules. 73-page course notes on Noetherian rings, unique factorization domains, and the structure theorem for modules over a PID.

title: Algebraic Topology Notes
note: Algebraic Topology Notes. 80-page notes on the fundamental group, covering spaces, singular homology, and the Mayer–Vietoris sequence.

title: Moduli Spaces in Algebraic Geometry
note: Moduli Spaces in Algebraic Geometry. Ravi Vakil's slides on representable functors, fine and coarse moduli spaces, and stack-theoretic criteria.

title: Course on Moduli Spaces
note: Course on Moduli Spaces. The homepage of Ravi Vakil's advanced algebraic geometry course on moduli spaces.

title: Principal Bundles with Formal Trivializations
note: Principal Bundles with Formal Trivializations. Slides on moduli of $G$-bundles on curves and Serre's theorem on linearization.

title: Teichmuller Flow and Complex Manifolds
note: Teichmuller Flow and Complex Manifolds. Vladimir Markovic's slides on extremal metrics, Teichmüller spaces, and hyperbolic dynamics.

title: The Orbit Method and Automorphic L-Functions
note: The Orbit Method and Automorphic L-Functions. Paul Nelson's slides on microlocal analysis on reductive groups, coadjoint orbits, Kirillov character formulas, branching coefficients, and the subconvexity problem.

title: Sheaf Models in Type Theory
note: Sheaf Models in Type Theory. Thierry Coquand's slides on constructive sheaf models of choice sequences and univalence.

title: Sheaf Theory in Machine Learning
note: Sheaf Theory in Machine Learning. Introduction to cellular sheaves, presheaves, and discrete Laplacians on graphs for data science.

title: Stacks of Shtukas and Geometric Langlands
note: Stacks of Shtukas and Geometric Langlands. Slides on the geometric Langlands correspondence for function fields. They use stacks of shtukas and local Shimura varieties.

title: Number Fields and Function Fields Analogy
note: Number Fields and Function Fields Analogy. Algorithmic aspects of the analogy between number rings $\mathcal{O}_K$ and function field curves $\mathbb{F}_q[C]$.

title: Introductory Number Fields
note: Introductory Number Fields. Elementary slides that introduce algebraic integers, norms, and ideal factorizations.

title: Surreal Numbers and Combinatorial Games
note: Surreal Numbers and Combinatorial Games. Introduction to Conway's surreal numbers as a totally ordered field. The field comes from transfinite game trees.

title: Function Fields and Curves
note: Function Fields and Curves. Summary of valuations, places, divisors, and the Riemann–Roch theorem for algebraic function fields.

title: Valuations and Places of Function Fields
note: Valuations and Places of Function Fields. Slides that give the details of discrete valuation rings, places, and the integral closure of curves.

title: History of the Hilbert Class Field
note: History of the Hilbert Class Field. Slides that follow the history of class field theory from Weber and Hilbert to Takagi and Artin.

title: Curves over Local and Global Fields
note: Curves over Local and Global Fields. Bjorn Poonen's complete survey on the arithmetic of curves, Jacobian varieties, and rational points.

title: Arithmetic Dynamics by Joseph Silverman
note: Arithmetic Dynamics by Joseph Silverman. ICM survey on heights, dynamical moduli spaces, and the arithmetic of rational maps.

title: Verdier Duality and Cosheaves
note: Verdier Duality and Cosheaves. Jacob Lurie's notes on cosheaves with compact support, the equivalence $\operatorname{Shv}(X)^\vee \cong \operatorname{CoShv}(X)$, and Poincaré–Verdier duality.

title: Introduction to Gerbes and Non-Abelian Cohomology
note: Introduction to Gerbes and Non-Abelian Cohomology. Ieke Moerdijk's notes. They give the definition of gerbes as stacks of non-empty, connected groupoids. Non-abelian Čech 2-cocycles $\check{H}^2(X, \mathcal{G})$ classify these gerbes.

title: The Isbell Adjunction by John Baez
note: The Isbell Adjunction by John Baez. Expository article on the duality between geometry (spaces) and algebra (functions) through the Isbell adjunction and the Yoneda/co-Yoneda lemmas.

title: Fontaine Theory and Number-Field Analogies
note: Fontaine Theory and Number-Field Analogies. A systematic dictionary that compares function fields over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and number fields through $p$-adic Hodge theory and Fontaine's period rings.

title: The Work of John Tate
note: The Work of John Tate. Milne's survey of Tate's contributions, which include Tate's thesis, the Tate conjecture, $p$-divisible groups, and Galois cohomology.

title: The Work of Goro Shimura
note: The Work of Goro Shimura. Milne's overview of Shimura's contributions to complex multiplication, modular forms, and Shimura varieties.

title: Simplicial Type Theory and Synthetic Higher Categories
note: Simplicial Type Theory and Synthetic Higher Categories. Formalization of the Yoneda lemma, Segal conditions, and Rezk types in simplicial homotopy type theory.

title: Brown Representability in Higher Categories
note: Brown Representability in Higher Categories. Akhil Mathew's exposition on the Brown representability theorem for stable $\infty$-categories and generalized cohomology functors.

title: The Yoneda Lemma in Homotopy Type Theory
note: The Yoneda Lemma in Homotopy Type Theory. Formalization of $\infty$-categories, right fibrations, covariance, and the $\infty$-categorical Yoneda lemma with synthetic type theory.

title: Gabriel-Ulmer Duality Notes
note: Gabriel-Ulmer Duality Notes. Slides on the 2-adjunction between finitely complete categories $\mathbf{LEX}^{\text{op}}$ and locally finitely presentable categories $\mathbf{LFP}$.

title: Giraud's Axioms for Topoi
note: Giraud's Axioms for Topoi. Jacob Lurie's lecture notes. They give a characterization of Grothendieck topoi as left-exact accessible localizations of presheaf categories.

title: Gabriel-Ulmer Duality for Infinity-Categories
note: Gabriel-Ulmer Duality for Infinity-Categories. Denis Nardin's proof. It factors Gabriel–Ulmer duality for $\infty$-categories through ind-completion $\operatorname{Ind}(-)$ and filtered colimits.

title: Duality of Theories and Models
note: Duality of Theories and Models. Gabriel–Ulmer duality as a natural equivalence between small finite-limit categories (theories) and locally presentable categories (models).

title: Tannakian Categories of Flat Connections
note: Tannakian Categories of Flat Connections. Construction of neutral Tannakian categories of vector bundles with flat connections and their relations to the étale fundamental group.

title: Tannaka Duality over Ring Spectra
note: Tannaka Duality over Ring Spectra. It gives Galois categories and neutral Tannakian duality over structured ring spectra. It identifies affine group schemes with spectral fundamental groups.

title: Étale Cohomology in the Stacks Project
note: Étale Cohomology in the Stacks Project. The foundational reference of more than 600 pages. It includes étale sites, proper base change, comparison theorems with singular cohomology, Poincaré duality, cycle classes, and the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula.

title: Elementary Proof of the Lefschetz Fixed Point Theorem
note: Elementary Proof of the Lefschetz Fixed Point Theorem. Exposition that links the Lefschetz number $L(f) = \sum (-1)^i \operatorname{Tr}(f_* | H_i)$ to mapping degrees and Euler characteristics.

title: Lorentzian Polynomials and Matroids
note: Lorentzian Polynomials and Matroids. June Huh's ICM plenary address on Lorentzian polynomials, log-concavity, Hodge theory for matroids, and generalized permutohedra.

title: Hermitian Symmetric Spaces and Shimura Varieties
note: Hermitian Symmetric Spaces and Shimura Varieties. J.S. Milne's classification of Riemannian and Hermitian symmetric domains and arithmetic quotients.

title: Notes on Differential Forms
note: Notes on Differential Forms. Donu Arapura's 53-page introduction to differential forms, exterior derivatives, Stokes' theorem, and de Rham cohomology.

title: Spreading Out and the Ax-Grothendieck Theorem
note: Spreading Out and the Ax-Grothendieck Theorem. Serre's note on the Ax–Grothendieck theorem: any injective polynomial endomorphism of $\mathbb{C}^n$ is surjective. The proof is a reduction to finite fields $\mathbb{F}_p$ through Nullstellensatz techniques.

title: Mod-2 Cohomological Invariants of Weyl Groups
note: Mod-2 Cohomological Invariants of Weyl Groups. Serre's calculation of the ring of mod-2 cohomological invariants for symmetric groups and Weyl groups.

title: Mod-p Reduction of Orthogonal Representations
note: Mod-p Reduction of Orthogonal Representations. Serre's paper shows that the mod-$p$ reduction of characteristic-zero orthogonal and symplectic representations stays orthogonal/symplectic for $p > 2$.

title: Subgroups of SO(3) and Platonic Symmetries
note: Subgroups of SO(3) and Platonic Symmetries. Serre's paper on finite subgroup embeddings $A_4 \cong \operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_3), S_4 \cong \operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_3), A_5 \cong \operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_5)$ in $\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathbb{R})$ and their applications.

title: The Geometry of Adeles and Lattices
note: The Geometry of Adeles and Lattices. Adelic interpretation of modular forms as functions on $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}) \backslash \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A})$. It shows that $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Q})$ is transitive on lattices in $\mathbb{Q}_p^n$ with stabilizer $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)$.

title: Valuation Rings in Scheme Theory
note: Valuation Rings in Scheme Theory. Definition of valuation rings through domination of local rings, and a characterization of directed colimits of valuation rings.

title: Algebraic K-Theory over the Field with One Element
note: Algebraic K-Theory over the Field with One Element. Deitmar's paper calculates the $K$-theory of $\mathbb{F}_1$ through Quillen's plus construction $B\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb{F}_1)^+$. It identifies $K_j(\mathbb{F}_1)$ with the stable homotopy groups of spheres $\pi_j^s(\mathbb{S})$.

title: Mellin Transforms and p-Adic Distributions
note: Mellin Transforms and p-Adic Distributions. $\mathbb{Z}_p$-valued measures, finitely additive distributions on compact opens, and $p$-adic Mellin transforms.

title: The Artin Map via Selmer K-Theory
note: The Artin Map via Selmer K-Theory. Dustin Clausen's paper interprets the Artin reciprocity map as a natural transformation from algebraic $K$-homology to topological $K$-homology. This applies to fields with virtual cohomological dimension $\operatorname{vcd}(F) \le 2$.

title: Dualities for Compact p-Adic Lie Groups
note: Dualities for Compact p-Adic Lie Groups. Clausen's revised thesis on Lazard–Poincaré duality and linearizations of $p$-adic Lie groups.

title: Short Primer on Galois Cohomology
note: Short Primer on Galois Cohomology. William Stein's concise notes about $H^0, H^1, H^2$, Hilbert's Theorem 90, and Brauer groups.

title: Higher Arithmetic Duality
note: Higher Arithmetic Duality. John Rognes on Poincaré duality, perfect cup product pairings $H^k \otimes H^{n-k} \to k$, and trace/evaluation maps in arithmetic topology.

title: The Ordinary Double Point and Monodromy
note: The Ordinary Double Point and Monodromy. Richard Thomas's visual notes on node singularities, vanishing cycles, and Picard–Lefschetz monodromy.

title: Vector Bundles and Chern Classes
note: Vector Bundles and Chern Classes. Richard Thomas's intuitive introduction to vector bundles, transition functions, clutching maps, the Möbius strip, and Chern classes $c_1(L) \in H^2(X, \mathbb{Z})$.

title: History of the Finite Simple Group Classification
note: History of the Finite Simple Group Classification. Solomon's historical survey of finite simple groups from Galois and Jordan to Sylow and the CFSG theorem.

title: Geometric Class Field Theory
