Key computation: classification of the number $r(n)$ of linearly independent vector fields on $S^{n-1}$ by the Radon–Hurwitz number $\rho(n)-1$: writing $n=(2a+1)\cdot2^{4b+c}$ with $c=0,1,2,3$, then $\rho(n)=2^c+8b$, and $\beta(n)=\rho(n)-1$ independent nowhere-vanishing fields exist, equality holding up to the $J$-image; concretely $\widetilde{KO}(\mathbb{RP}^n)=\mathbb{Z}/2^c\oplus\mathbb{Z}/2^{\lceil n/2\rceil}$ computed from $KO(\mathbb{CP}^n)=\mathbb{Z}[u]/(u^{n+1})$.

title: Caleb Ji
note: Caleb Ji, spectra and the stable homotopy category. Key computation: the homotopy groups of a spectrum $X$ are $\pi_k(X)=\mathrm{colim}_n\pi_{k+n}(X_n)$, and the smash product $X\wedge Y$ with latching structure $(X\wedge Y)_n=(X\wedge Y)_n^{\mathrm{lat}}\cup\cdots$ shows $S^0\wedge S^0=S^0$ gives $\pi_*(S)$ as the initial stable homotopy ring.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, derived algebraic geometry foundations and higher stacks. Key computation: for the derived zero locus $X=s^{-1}(0)$ of a section $s$ of a vector bundle $E\to V$, $L_X\simeq[E^*|_X\xrightarrow{Ds}T^*V|_X]$, perfect in degrees $[-1,0]$; explicitly $A^*=K[z_1..z_n,y_1..y_m,x_1..x_l]$ with $\deg z=0,\deg y=-1,\deg x=-2$, $dy_j=f_j(z)$, $dx_i=\sum_j g_{ij}(z)y_j$, $d^2=0$ forcing $\sum_j g_{ij}(z)f_j(z)=0$, so $H^0(A^*)=K[z]/(f_1=0,..,f_m=0)$ classifies the classical truncation $X=t_0(X)\subset\mathbb{A}^n$, with $L_X\simeq[\mathcal{O}_X^m\xrightarrow{\partial f_j/\partial z_k}\mathcal{O}_X^n]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$.

title: Raphaël Ponge
note: Raphaël Ponge, semiclassical analysis on spectral triples extending the semiclassical Weyl law and Connes' integration formula to $p$-summable spectral triples without Hölder-regularity. Key computation: the semiclassical Weyl law $\lim_{h\to0^+}h^n N^-(h^2\Delta_g+V)=\int_M V_-(x)^{n/2}\,d\nu_g(x)$ (and $\lim h^n N^-(h^{2q}\Delta_g^q+V)=\int V_-^{n/2q}$); the main theorem — if for all $a\in A$, $a>0$, $\lim_{j\to\infty}j^{-2/p}\lambda_j(aD^2a)=\tau(a^{-p/2})$, then $\lim_{j}j^{-2/p}\lambda_j(|D|^{-q/2}a|D|^{-q/2})=\tau(a^{q/p})$ for all $q>0$, and for $V^*=V\in A$, $\lim_{h\to0^+}h^p N^-(h^2D^2+V)=\mathrm{Res}_{z=p}\,\mathrm{Tr}(V_-)^{z/2}|D|^{-z}$, recovering Connes' integration formula $\int f=\mathrm{Res}_{z=p}\mathrm{Tr}(f|D|^{-z})$.

title: chromatic homotopy seminar notes
note: chromatic homotopy seminar notes, the nilpotence theorem and the thick subcategory theorem (Devinatz–Hopkins–Smith). Key computation: Theorem 9 (Hopkins–Smith) classifies thick subcategories of finite $p$-local spectra as exactly the $\mathcal{C}_{\ge n}=\{X:K(m)_*(X)=0\text{ for }m<n\}$; the Nilpotence theorem states $MU$ detects nilpotence ($x\in\pi_*(R)$ nilpotent iff $MU_*x$ nilpotent iff $MU_*x=0$ in $MU_*R$), so a self-map $f$ vanishing on $K(n)_0R$ forces $f$ nilpotent, and the enumeration proceeds by showing $C_{n+1}\subsetneq C_n$ is proper via Morava $K$-acyclicity.

title: Constantin Teleman
note: Constantin Teleman, chromatic spectral sequence and stable homotopy of the spheres seminar notes: develops the $MU$-Adams (chromatic) spectral sequence $E_2=H^*(M_{fg},\omega^*)$ and computes $\pi_*L_{K(1)}S$. Key computation: for $S_1=\mathbb{G}_m(\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge)$, $(E_1)_*=\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge[u^{\pm1}]$; splitting $S_1=C_{p-1}\times\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge$ ($p$ odd), $H^*(C_{p-1};\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge[u^{\pm1}])=\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge[u^{\pm(p-1)}]$, and $H^i(\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge;A)=\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge/(kp)$ for $i=2k(p-1)-1$, $k\ne0$, else $0$; the truncated chromatic spectral sequence gives the $E(q)$-local sphere agreeing with true stable stems within a finite, monotonically increasing radius (chromatic convergence), with stabilizer group $S_q\subset O_q=\mathbb{F}_{p^q}\langle S\rangle/(S^q=p,\,Sw=w^\varphi S)$ and $L_{K(n)}S\simeq E_n^{hS_n}$.

title: facets of spectral algebraic geometry seminar notes (KTH/SU): spectra as $S$-modules
note: facets of spectral algebraic geometry seminar notes (KTH/SU): spectra as $S$-modules, $THH(A)=A\otimes^*_S A$, $TC^t$ the $S^1$-equivariant refinement, and $MP$ (the 2-periodization of $MU$) as an affine chart for the moduli stack of oriented spectral formal groups. Key computation: $\pi_*MU\cong L$, the Lazard ring, so formal groups over $R$ are classified by $L\to R$, and $E^*(X)=MU^*(X)\otimes_{MU^*(*)}E^*(*)$ defines a cohomology theory iff $(p,v_1^{(p)},...,v_n^{(p)})$ is regular in $E^*(*)$ for all $p,n$ (Landweber), equivalently $\mathrm{Spec}\,R\to M_{fg}$ flat, classifying Landweber-exact theories as flat families over the moduli stack of formal groups.

title: Bhargav Bhatt
note: Bhargav Bhatt, perfectoid spaces via inversions/tilting, developing the tilting correspondence and almost purity in dimension 0 and in characteristic $p$. Key computation: Theorem 3.2.8 — for a perfectoid field $K$, the tilt $L\mapsto L^\flat$ induces an equivalence of finite-étale categories $\hat{K}_{\text{ét}}\simeq \hat{K}^\flat_{\text{ét}}$, i.e. finite extensions of $K$ are classified by finite extensions of $K^\flat$; concretely $\mathbb{Z}_p^\flat\cong\mathbb{F}_p((t^{1/p^\infty}))$, with the chain $\mathrm{Perf}_K\simeq\mathrm{Perf}_{K^{\circ a}}\simeq\mathrm{Perf}_{K^{\circ a}/\pi}$ implemented by $R\mapsto R^{\circ a}$, $A\mapsto A^*/[1/t]$, $A\mapsto A/\pi$.

title: Krauze
note: Krauze, prismatic envelopes and an explicit algorithm computing $\mathbb{Z}_p(i)(O_K/\varpi^n)$. Key computation: for $A=W(k)[[z]]$, $R=O_K/\varpi^n=A/(E(z),z^n)$, the prismatic envelope $\Delta_{R/A}=(A\{a\}/(da-r)_\delta)^\wedge_{p,d}$ is free over $R$ on monomials $\prod(\delta^u a)^{e_u}$ with $e_u<p$, and $\mathbb{Z}_p(i)(R)$ is the fiber of $\mathrm{can}-\varphi$ on the double complex over $\Delta_{R/\mathbb{Z}_p[[z_0,z_1]]}$; using the staircase bases $z^kd^c\prod f_u^{e_u}$ ($c+p^ue_u\ge i$) and a comparison lemma for differing differentials, Theorem 5.1 gives $|H^1(\mathbb{Z}_p(i)(O_K/\varpi^n))|/|H^2(\mathbb{Z}_p(i)(O_K/\varpi^n))|=q^{(n-1)i}$, hence $|K_{2i-1}(O_K/\varpi^n)|/|K_{2i-2}(O_K/\varpi^n)|=q^{(n-1)i}(q^i-1)$, and Theorem 5.2 gives even vanishing $K_{2i-2}(O_K/\varpi^n)=0$ for $i\gg0$.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, obstruction theories, virtual classes, and invariants: constructs virtual fundamental classes for quasi-smooth derived schemes. Key computation: for $X=s^{-1}(0)$ the derived zero locus of a section $s:V\to E$ with $V$ smooth and $E$ a vector bundle, $L_X\simeq[E^*|_X\xrightarrow{Ds}T^*V|_X]$, $\mathrm{vdim}(X)=\dim(V)-\mathrm{rank}(E)$, and $[X]^{\mathrm{virt}}=[V]\cap c_{\mathrm{rank}(E)}(E)$; for plane curves $C,D\subset\mathbb{CP}^2$ of degrees $m,n$ this gives the virtual intersection number $mn$ even when $C\cap D$ is not transverse.

title: Jiantong Liu
note: Jiantong Liu, categorifying spectra: explains the Ramzi–Sosnilo–Winges construction showing every spectrum occurs as nonconnective $K$-theory of a small idempotent-complete stable $\infty$-category. Key computation: the Dundas–McCarthy linearization is $M\simeq\mathrm{colim}_n\Omega^n\widetilde{K}(\mathrm{Sp}^\omega;\Sigma^nM)$; identifying this colimit as $K(C_M)$ yields $K(C_M)\simeq M$ functorially, and the resulting examples show the nonconnective theorem-of-the-heart map $K(E^\heartsuit)\to K(E)$ can fail without the Noetherian hypothesis.

title: algebraic topology lecture notes
note: algebraic topology lecture notes, an explicit Tor calculation extracting torsion. Key computation: for $R=\mathbb{Z}$ and $M=\mathbb{Z}/n$, the free resolution $0\to\mathbb{Z}\xrightarrow{n}\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}/n\to0$ gives $\mathbb{Z}/n\otimes N\cong N/nN$ and $\mathrm{Tor}_1^{\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{Z}/n,N)\cong\ker(n:N\to N)$, so $\mathrm{Tor}_1$ extracts exactly the $n$-torsion of $N$.

title: Stefan Schwede
note: Stefan Schwede, universal symmetries: global equivariant homotopy theory packages compatible equivariant homotopy theories for all compact Lie groups into global spectra and global Mackey functors. Key computation: $\pi_0^G(\mathbb{S})$ is the Burnside ring $A(G)$, freely generated by transfers $\mathrm{tr}_H^G(1)$ over conjugacy classes of closed $H\le G$ with finite Weyl group; the unit $\mathbb{S}\to KU$ sends a finite $G$-set to its permutation representation, giving the homomorphism $A(G)\to R(G)$.

title: Jiwu Jang
note: Jiwu Jang, vertex functions of type D Nakajima quiver varieties: proves a product expression for type-$D$ vertex functions in terms of $q$-binomial factors indexed by roots. Key computation: for the $D_4$ quiver with dimension vector $v=(1,2,1,1)$ and framing $w=(0,0,0,1)$, the vertex function factors into $q$-binomial-series terms associated to specific $D_4$ roots; in the $D_1$ case $V(z)=\sum_{k\ge0}(\hbar)_k/(q)_k\cdot z^k$, the ordinary $q$-binomial series.

title: Vesselin Dimitrov (joint with Frank Calegari and Yunqing Tang)
note: Vesselin Dimitrov (joint with Frank Calegari and Yunqing Tang), arithmetic holonomy bounds and special values of $L$-functions: proves $\mathbb{Q}$-linear independence results for $1,\zeta(2)$, and $L(2,\chi_{-3})$ using Apéry-style $G$-functions and modular periods. Key computation: with the Picard–Fuchs operator $L=x(1-x)(1-9x)d^2/dx^2+(1-20x+27x^2)d/dx+(9x-3)$, the chosen functions satisfy $L(A)=0$, $L(AB)=1$, and $L(AC)=1/(1-x)$; the Apéry limits identify $L(2,\chi_{-3})/2$ and $\zeta(2)/4$ as $w_6$-periods, producing simultaneous rational approximants.

title: Gabriel Dospinescu
note: Gabriel Dospinescu, overview of the Fargues–Fontaine curve presenting the classification of vector bundles and its diamond-theoretic construction. Key computation: for $S=\mathrm{Spa}(C)$ geometric, every rank-$n$ vector bundle on $X_C$ is uniquely classified by a nonincreasing slope sequence $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\in\mathbb{Q}$ through $\mathcal{E}\simeq\bigoplus_i\mathcal{O}(\lambda_i)$, equivalently by $B(\mathrm{GL}_n)$; this follows from $X_S=Y_S/\varphi^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and, for the pullback $\mathcal{F}$ to the Stein space $Y_S$, the two-term computation $R\Gamma(X_S,\mathcal{E})\simeq[\mathcal{F}(Y_S)\xrightarrow{1-\varphi}\mathcal{F}(Y_S)]$, so $H^i(X_S,\mathcal{E})=0$ for $i>1$.

title: Alain Connes (joint with Caterina Consani)
note: Alain Connes (joint with Caterina Consani), from noncommutative geometry to tropical geometry: develops the arithmetic site and a tropical Riemann–Roch theory for the scaling quotient $C_p=\mathbb{R}_+^*/p^{\mathbb{Z}}$. Key computation: for $p>2$, principal divisors lie in the kernel of degree and the pair $(\deg,\chi)$ gives $\mathrm{Div}(C_p)/\mathcal{P}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{Z}/(p-1)\mathbb{Z}$; with $H^0(D)_\rho=\{f\in H^0(D):\lVert f\rVert_p\le\rho\}$ and $\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb{R}}H^0(D)=\lim_{n\to\infty}p^{-n}\dim_{\mathrm{top}}H^0(D)^{p^n}$, the slides compute $\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb{R}}H^0(D)-\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb{R}}H^0(-D)=\deg D$.

title: Bertrand Toën
note: Bertrand Toën, derived algebraic geometry and deformation quantization: explains the canonical $(2-d)$-quantization of the derived stack $\mathrm{Bun}_G(X)$ for a compact oriented $d$-manifold (or Calabi–Yau variety). Key computation: at a $G$-bundle $E$, $T_{\mathrm{Bun}_G(X),E}\simeq C^*(X,\mathrm{ad}(E))[1]$; cup product followed by the invariant pairing on $\mathfrak{g}$ and integration over $X$ produces a nondegenerate closed 2-form of degree $2-d$, hence a $(2-d)$-shifted Poisson structure, while higher formality identifies deformations of $D_{\mathrm{qcoh}}(Z)$ as an $E_n$-monoidal dg-category with the dg Lie algebra $R\Gamma(Z,\mathrm{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_Z}(T_Z[-1-n]))[n+1]$, yielding the quantization.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, triangulated categories and derived categories: culminates in the Fourier–Mukai classification of exact functors between derived categories of smooth projective schemes. Key computation: a kernel $\mathcal{E}^\bullet\in D^b\mathrm{coh}(X\times Y)$ defines $\Phi_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathcal{G}^\bullet)=R(\pi_Y)_*(L\pi_X^*\mathcal{G}^\bullet\otimes^L\mathcal{E}^\bullet)$; Mukai's formulas give its adjoints using $D_{X\times Y}(\mathcal{E}^\bullet)\otimes^L\pi_Y^*K_Y[\dim Y]$ and $D_{X\times Y}(\mathcal{E}^\bullet)\otimes^L\pi_X^*K_X[\dim X]$, and Orlov's theorem identifies every exact functor $D^b\mathrm{coh}(X)\to D^b\mathrm{coh}(Y)$ with left and right adjoints with a unique such kernel up to isomorphism.

title: Jonathan Wang (joint with Tony Feng)
note: Jonathan Wang (joint with Tony Feng), geometric periods: categorifies the $\mathrm{GL}_2$ period formula and proves matching filtrations on its spectral and automorphic objects under geometric Langlands. Key computation: for $\check{X}=\mathrm{std}=\mathbb{A}^2$ and $X=\mathbb{G}_m\backslash\mathrm{GL}_2$, the two $\check{G}$-orbits $\{0\}$ and $\mathbb{A}^2\setminus\{0\}=\check{G}/\check{\mathrm{Mir}}_2$ yield the distinguished triangle $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{std}}\to\Pi^{\mathrm{spec}}_*(\omega_{\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{X}/\check{G}}})\to\mathrm{Eis}^{\mathrm{spec}}_{\check{\mathrm{Mir}}_2}(\omega_{\mathrm{LocSys}_{\mathbb{G}_m}})\xrightarrow{[1]}$, whose first term has !-stalk $\mathrm{Sym}\,H^\bullet_{\mathrm{dR}}(C,E)$; unfolding produces the matching automorphic triangle with $T_{\mathrm{Sym}(\mathrm{std})}(\mathrm{Whit})$, $\Pi_!(\mathbb{C}_{\mathrm{Bun}_X})$, and $\mathrm{Eis}_{\mathrm{Mir}_2,!}(\mathbb{C}_{\mathrm{Bun}_{\mathbb{G}_m}})$.

title: Sanath K
note: Sanath K. Devalapurkar, equivariant homotopy theory and geometric Langlands: proves generalized derived Satake equivalences with periodic and elliptic cohomology coefficients. Key computation: for simply connected, simply laced semisimple $G$, $\mathrm{Shv}_G^c(\Omega G;KU)\otimes\mathbb{Q}\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}(\check{G}_{\mathrm{sc}}/\check{G})_{\text{2-per}}$, replacing the rational equivalence $\mathrm{Shv}_G^c(\Omega G;\mathbb{Q})\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{g}}^*/\check{G})$; for an elliptic theory $A$ with curve $E$, this becomes $\mathrm{Shv}_{G/Z(G)}^c(\Omega G;A)\otimes\mathbb{Q}\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}(\mathrm{Bun}^{\mathrm{ss},0}_{\check{G}}(E))\otimes_{\pi_0A}\pi_*(A_{\mathbb{Q}})$, identifying the spectral moduli object from the coefficient theory's formal group.

title: Shachar Carmeli
note: Shachar Carmeli, cyclotomic redshift: presents chromatic cyclotomic extensions and their height-raising behavior under algebraic $K$-theory. Key computation: the splitting $S_{T(n)}[B^nC_{p^k}]\simeq S_{T(n)}[B^nC_{p^{k-1}}]\times S_{T(n)}[\omega_{p^k}^{(n)}]$ defines a $(\mathbb{Z}/p^k)^\times$-Galois extension, and for every commutative $T(n)$-local ring spectrum $R$ the redshift equivalence $L_{T(n+1)}K(R[\omega_{p^k}^{(n)}])\simeq L_{T(n+1)}K(R)[\omega_{p^k}^{(n+1)}]$ raises its chromatic height; passing to the tower gives cyclotomic hyperdescent $L_{K(n+1)}K(R[\omega_{p^\infty}^{(n)}])^{h\mathbb{Z}}\simeq L_{K(n+1)}K(R)$.

title: Franz Luef
note: Franz Luef, noncommutative geometry and time-frequency analysis: identifies well-localized Gabor frames with projective modules and explicit projections over noncommutative tori. Key computation: the Feichtinger module $M_s^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ is an equivalence bimodule between $A_s^1(\alpha\mathbb{Z}\times\beta\mathbb{Z},c)$ and $A_s^1(\alpha^{-1}\mathbb{Z}\times\beta^{-1}\mathbb{Z},c)$ via the associativity identity ${}_\Lambda\langle f,g\rangle h=f\langle g,h\rangle_{\Lambda^\circ}$; a Gabor atom satisfies $p_g={}_\Lambda\langle g,g\rangle$, with $p_g^2=p_g=p_g^*$ exactly when $g\langle g,g\rangle_{\Lambda^\circ}=g$, and the canonical tight atom $h_0=S_{g,g}^{-1/2}g$ yields such a projection, existing for rectangular $\Lambda=\alpha\mathbb{Z}\times\beta\mathbb{Z}$ precisely when $\alpha\beta<1$.

title: Linus Hamann
note: Linus Hamann, compatibility of the Fargues–Scholze and Gan–Takeda local Langlands parameters for $\mathrm{GSp}_4$ and its inner form in the stated unramified $p>2$ cases. Key computation: for a stable supercuspidal parameter $\phi$ with packets $\Pi_\phi(G)=\{\pi\}$ and $\Pi_\phi(J)=\{\rho\}$, local-shtuka cohomology is $R\Gamma_c(G,b,\mu)[\pi]\simeq\rho\otimes(\mathrm{std}\circ\phi)^\vee\otimes|\cdot|^{-3/2}[-3]$ and $R\Gamma_c(G,b,\mu)[\rho]\simeq\pi\otimes(\mathrm{std}\circ\phi)\otimes|\cdot|^{-3/2}[-3]$; for endoscopic $\mathrm{std}\circ\phi\simeq\phi_1\oplus\phi_2$, the two packet members pair with the corresponding $\phi_i$ summands.

title: Guozhen Wang (joint with Ruochuan Liu)
note:
Guozhen Wang (joint with Ruochuan Liu), topological cyclic homology of local fields: computes the descent spectral sequences for $THH$, $TP$, and $TC$ of a local field's integers. Key computation: for $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ with ramification index $e$ and $d=[K(\zeta_p):K]$, the slides obtain a Bott class $\beta\in E_2^{0,2d}(TC(\mathcal{O}_K);\mathbb{F}_p)$ and $E_2^{0,*}\cong\mathbb{F}_p[\beta]$, $E_2^{1,*}\cong\mathbb{F}_p[\beta]\{\lambda,\gamma\}\oplus k[\beta]\{\alpha_i^{(j)}\mid1\le i\le e,1\le j\le d\}$, $E_2^{2,*}\cong\mathbb{F}_p[\beta]\{\lambda\gamma\}$, and $E_2^{i,*}=0$ for $i\ge3$, forcing the descent spectral sequence to collapse.
https://raphaelponge.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/berkeley_ncg4.pdf, Raphaël Ponge, the Connes–Chern character of a finitely summable spectral triple pairs with projective-module $K$-theory to recover the Fredholm index, and for the noncommutative torus is represented by its fundamental cyclic $2$-cocycle. Key computation: for $E=eA^q$ and $k\geq p/2$, $\operatorname{ind}D_{\nabla^E}=\frac12\operatorname{Str}(D^{-1}[D,e])^{2k+1}=\langle\operatorname{Ch}(D),\operatorname{Ch}(E)\rangle$; for $A_\theta$, $HP_0(A_\theta)=\langle\tau_0,\tau_2\rangle$ with $\tau_2(a^0,a^1,a^2)=\tau_0(a^0(\delta_1(a^1)\delta_2(a^2)-\delta_2(a^1)\delta_1(a^2)))$, giving the index pairing explicitly.

title: Raphaël Ponge (joint with Hang Wang)
note: Raphaël Ponge (joint with Hang Wang), conformal deformation produces a twisted spectral triple whose Connes–Chern character is conformally invariant and is computed by a fixed-point local index cocycle. Key computation: $\widehat g=k^{-2}g$ gives $(C^\infty(M),L^2_{\widehat g}(M,S),D_{\widehat g})\simeq(C^\infty(M),L^2_g(M,S),\sqrt{k}D_g\sqrt{k})$ and, for the crossed product $C^\infty(M)\rtimes G$, $\sigma_g(fu_\phi)=k_\phi^{-1}fu_\phi$; for a $G$-invariant $g$, $\operatorname{Ch}(D_g)_{\sigma_g}$ is represented by $\varphi_{2m}(f^0u_{\phi_0},\ldots,f^{2m}u_{\phi_{2m}})=\frac{(-i)^{n/2}}{(2m)!}\sum_a(2\pi)^{-a/2}\int_{M_a^\phi}\widehat A(R^{TM_a^\phi})\wedge\nu_\phi(R^{N^\phi})\wedge f^0d\widehat f^1\wedge\cdots\wedge d\widehat f^{2m}$.

title: Nitin Nitsure
note: Nitin Nitsure, cotangent-complex Ext groups classify square-zero deformation problems for schemes, morphisms, and coherent sheaves and supply Artin-style tangent–obstruction data for algebraic moduli stacks. Key computation: for a flat $f:Y\to X$ and a square-zero extension $X\hookrightarrow X'$ with ideal $I$, the transitivity triangle $f^*L_{X/X'}\to L_{Y/X'}\to L_{Y/X}\xrightarrow{[1]}$ yields $0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(L_{Y/X},f^*I)\to\operatorname{Exal}(Y/X',f^*I)\to\operatorname{End}(f^*I)\xrightarrow{\partial}\operatorname{Ext}^2(L_{Y/X},f^*I)$; the obstruction is $\partial(\operatorname{id}_{f^*I})$, lifts form a torsor under $\operatorname{Ext}^1$, and infinitesimal automorphisms are $\operatorname{Ext}^0$.

title: Avi Zeff
note: Avi Zeff, prisms deperfect perfectoid geometry while prismatic cohomology recovers crystalline cohomology and equips quasiregular semiperfectoid rings with an explicit Nygaard filtration. Key computation: $R\mapsto(A_{\inf}(R),\ker\theta)$ and $(A,I)\mapsto A/I$ give inverse equivalences between perfectoid rings and perfect prisms; for a crystalline prism $(A,I)$, $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{crys}}(R/A)\simeq\varphi^*\Delta_{R/A}=\Delta_{R/A}\widehat\otimes^L_{A,\varphi_A}A$, while for quasiregular semiperfectoid $R$ the site has initial prism $(\Delta_R^{\mathrm{init}},(d))$, so $\Delta_R=\Delta_R^{\mathrm{init}}$ is concentrated in degree $0$ and $N^{\geq i}\Delta_R=\varphi^{-1}(d^i\Delta_R)$.

title: Raphaël Ponge
note: Raphaël Ponge, Connes' trace theorem identifies the Dixmier-trace noncommutative integral of an order-$-n$ pseudodifferential operator with its Wodzicki residue, recovering Riemannian volume spectrally. Key computation: Weyl's law gives $\lambda_k(\Delta_g)\sim(k/(c_n\operatorname{Vol}_gM))^{2/n}$, hence $\Delta_g^{-n/2}$ is measurable and $\operatorname{Tr}_\omega(\Delta_g^{-n/2})=c_n\operatorname{Vol}_g(M)$; more generally, for $P\in\Psi^{-n}(M)$, $\operatorname{Tr}_\omega(P)=\frac1n\operatorname{Res}(P)$, so $\operatorname{Tr}_\omega(f\Delta_g^{-n/2})=c_n\int_M f(x)\sqrt{g(x)}\,d^nx$.

title: Raphaël Ponge
note: Raphaël Ponge, the irrational noncommutative torus admits an explicit Dirac spectral triple, while conformal weights produce twisted spectral triples and a conformally invariant zeta value. Key computation: $A_\theta=\{\sum_{m,n}a_{m,n}U^mV^n:(a_{m,n})\in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{Z}^2)\}$ with $VU=e^{-2\pi i\theta}UV$, $\partial=\delta_1+i\delta_2$, and $D=\begin{psmallmatrix}0&\partial^*\\ \partial&0\end{psmallmatrix}$ is isospectral to $\partial+\partial^*$ on $\mathbb{T}^2$; a Weyl factor $k>0$ gives $\sigma(a)=k^{-1}ak$ and the twisted triple $(A_\theta^{\mathrm{op}},H_\varphi,D_\varphi)_\sigma$, for which $\zeta(\Delta_\varphi;0)$ is independent of $\varphi(a)=\tau_0(ak^{-2})$.

title: Raphaël Ponge
note: Raphaël Ponge, the $(b,B)$ mixed complex identifies periodic cyclic homology of smooth functions with de Rham cohomology and gives an explicit cyclic-homology Chern character for projective modules. Key computation: the HKR map $\alpha(f^0\otimes\cdots\otimes f^m)=\frac1{m!}f^0df^1\wedge\cdots\wedge df^m$ intertwines $(b,B)$ with $(0,d)$, yielding $HP_0(C^\infty(M))\simeq H^{\mathrm{ev}}(M)$ and $HP_1(C^\infty(M))\simeq H^{\mathrm{odd}}(M)$; for $E\simeq eA^q$, $\operatorname{Ch}_{2k}(e)=(-1)^k\frac{(2k)!}{k!}\operatorname{Tr}((e-\frac12)\otimes e^{\otimes 2k})$ satisfies $(b+B)\operatorname{Ch}(e)=0$ and depends only on $E$.

title: Thomas Nikolaus
note: Thomas Nikolaus, Frobenius maps in higher algebra turn topological Hochschild homology into a computable cyclotomic object and identify prismatic graded pieces of relative $\mathrm{THH}$ and $\mathrm{TC}$. Key computation: the Tate diagonal and multiplication give $\varphi_p:R\to(R^{\otimes_S p})^{tC_p}\to R^{tC_p}$ and $\varphi_p:\mathrm{THH}(R)\to\mathrm{THH}(R)^{tC_p}$; for connective $R$, $\mathrm{TC}(R)\simeq\operatorname{map}_{\mathrm{CycSp}}(\mathbbm{1},\mathrm{THH}(R))$, while for a prism $(A,I)$ and $R=A/I$ ultimate Bökstedt periodicity computes $\mathrm{THH}_*(R/S_A)\cong I^n/I^{n+1}$ in degree $2n$ and $0$ in odd degrees, and the complete filtration on $\mathrm{TC}(R/S_A)$ has graded pieces $\mathbb{Z}_p(i)(R/A)[2i]$.

title: Seokbeom Yoon (joint with Stavros Garoufalidis)
note: Seokbeom Yoon (joint with Stavros Garoufalidis), twisted Neumann–Zagier matrices compute twisted loop invariants of finite cyclic covers and force higher-loop asymptotic multiplicativity. Key computation: from $A(t)=G(t)-G'(t)$ and $B(t)=G''(t)-G(t)$ one has $A(t)B(1/t)^T=B(t)A(1/t)^T$; the twisted one-loop invariant is $\Phi_{1,M}(t)=\frac12\det(A(t)\operatorname{diag}(z_1'',\ldots,z_N'')+B(t)\operatorname{diag}(z_1^{-1},\ldots,z_N^{-1}))$, and for the $n$-cyclic cover $\Phi_{1,M^{(n)}}=\prod_{\omega^n=1}\Phi_{1,M}(\omega)$; for $M=S^3\setminus4_1$, $\Phi_{2,M^{(n)}}=\frac{55\sqrt3}{1512}n-\frac{8\sqrt3\,n}{63(1-\lambda^n)}+\frac{8\sqrt3\,n}{63(1-\lambda^n)^2}\sim\frac{55\sqrt3}{1512}n$, where $\lambda=(7+3\sqrt5)/2$ is a root of $\Phi_{1,M}(t)$.

title: William Balderrama
note: William Balderrama, Borel-completed Morava theory supplies an equivariant $K(n)$-local sphere whose localization agrees with the explicit cofree construction, with a descent route to $RO(G)$-graded computations. Key computation: for a finite $p$-group the Segal conjecture gives $S_G^{\wedge_p}\simeq b_G(S)$ and $b_G(S_{K(n)})=b_G(E_n)^{h\mathbb{G}_n}$, with $H_c^*(K;\pi_?b_G(E_n))\Longrightarrow\pi_?b_G(E_n^{hK})$ and $\pi_\alpha b_G(E_n)=E_n^0\operatorname{Th}(\alpha)$; taking $K(n)_G=b_G(K(n))$ yields $L_{b_G(K(n))}S_G\simeq b_G(S_{K(n)})$, while at height one $KU_G/(p)\simeq b_G(KU/(p))$ and the explicit $C_2$ calculation has $KO_{C_2}/(\eta_{C_2})\simeq KR$.

title: N
note: N. Christopher Phillips, algebraic, topological, and operator-algebraic $K$-theory share the projective-module construction, which becomes a periodic cohomology theory for Banach algebras. Key computation: Swan's equivalence $\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbb{C}}(X)\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathrm{fg}}(C(X))$ identifies $K^0(X)=K_0(C(X))=G(V(X))$; concretely $V(A)$ is the monoid of stable Murray--von Neumann classes of idempotents in $M_\infty(A)$, and for $A=\mathcal{L}(\ell^2)$ one has $V(A)\cong\{0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$ with $n+\infty=\infty$, hence $K_0(A)=0$; Bott periodicity $K_0(SA)\cong K_1(A)$ and $K_1(SA)\cong K_0(A)$ then converts an extension $0\to J\to A\to A/J\to0$ into the six-term exact sequence in $K$-theory.

title: Raphaël Ponge
note: Raphaël Ponge, the Atiyah--Singer formula becomes the $K$-theoretic index pairing of the Dirac spectral triple, extending verbatim to finitely generated projective modules over a noncommutative algebra. Key computation: for a compact even-dimensional spin manifold and a bundle $E$, the twisted Dirac operator satisfies $\operatorname{ind}D_E=(2\pi i)^{-n/2}\int_M\widehat A(R^M)\wedge\operatorname{Ch}(F^E)$; Serre--Swan writes $E=eC^\infty(M)^q$ and identifies $D_E$ with $e(D\otimes1)e$, so the spectral triple $(A,H,D)$ sends $eA^q$ to the Fredholm operator $D_E=e(D\otimes1)e$ and defines $\operatorname{ind}_D:K_0(A)\to\mathbb{Z}$, recovering $\operatorname{ind}_D[E]=(2\pi i)^{-n/2}\langle\widehat A(R^M)^\vee,E\rangle$ when $A=C^\infty(M)$.

title: Eva Viehmann (joint with Kieu Hieu Nguyen)
note: Eva Viehmann (joint with Kieu Hieu Nguyen), modifications of the trivial $G$-bundle on the Fargues--Fontaine curve admit a canonical Harder--Narasimhan reduction, stratifying the $B_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-Grassmannian and relating weak admissibility to Newton strata. Key computation: Beauville--Laszlo gluing gives $\mathrm{BL}:\mathrm{Gr}_G\to\mathrm{Bun}_G$, and for $x\in\mathrm{Gr}_G(C)$ the unique parabolic $P\subset G$ has a $P$-dominant slope vector $v_P$ with semistable Levi modification; this defines the lower semicontinuous map $\mathrm{HN}:|\mathrm{Gr}_{G,\mu}|\to B(G,\mu)$, satisfying $\mathrm{HN}(x)\le[(b')^{-1}]$ on the Newton stratum where $\mathcal{E}_{1,x}\simeq\mathcal{E}_{b'}$, while for classical $x\in\mathrm{Gr}_{G,\mu}(K)$ equality $\mathrm{HN}(x)=[(b')^{-1}]=\mathrm{HN}_{\mathrm{DOR}}(\mathrm{BB}_\mu(x))$ identifies the classical semistable and basic loci.

title: Xu Shen (joint with Miaofen Chen and Laurent Fargues)
note: Xu Shen (joint with Miaofen Chen and Laurent Fargues), the Fargues--Rapoport conjecture classifies exactly when the admissible and weakly admissible $p$-adic period domains coincide. Key computation: a point $x\in\mathcal{F}(G,\mu)(C)$ modifies the Fargues bundle $\mathcal{E}_b$ at $\infty$ to $\mathcal{E}_{b,x}$, giving $\mathcal{F}(G,\mu,b)^a(C)=\{x\mid\mathcal{E}_{b,x}\simeq\mathcal{E}_1\}$; for basic $[b_0]\in B(G,\mu)$, one proves $\mathcal{F}(G,\mu,b_0)^a=\mathcal{F}(G,\mu,b_0)^{wa}$ iff $(G,\{\mu\})$ is fully Hodge--Newton decomposable, meaning each nonbasic $[b']\in B(G,\mu)$ has a Newton--Hodge contact point that is a break of the Newton polygon and reduces the datum to a proper Levi, with examples including $(\mathrm{GL}_h,(1,0,\ldots,0))$ and $(\mathrm{GSp}_4,(1,1,0,0))$.

title: Kiran S
note: Kiran S. Kedlaya, the Fargues--Fontaine curve converts $p$-adic Galois representations and relative étale local systems into semistable degree-zero vector bundles from which étale and de Rham realizations can be recovered. Key computation: with $P=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}B^{\varphi=p^n}$, $X_{FF}=\operatorname{Proj}(P)$ is regular, connected, noetherian, and one-dimensional, and $\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}^{\mathrm{cont}}(G_{\mathbb{Q}_p})\simeq\operatorname{Bun}^{\Gamma,\mathrm{ss},\mu=0}(X_{FF})$; for a perfect Banach $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra $R$, the relative construction $P_R=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}B_R^{\varphi=p^n}$ yields natural equivalences between étale $\mathbb{Q}_p$-local systems on $\mathcal{M}(R)$, those on $\mathcal{M}(\widetilde R)$, and fibrewise semistable degree-zero bundles on $\operatorname{Proj}(P_R)$, while the global $\Gamma$-fixed sections and the completed local fraction field at the de Rham point recover étale and de Rham cohomology respectively.

title: J
note: J. P. Pridham, smooth pro-Banach completion of algebraic $K$-theory is computed by real Deligne cohomology, refining the gap between discrete algebraic and topological $K$-theory. Key computation: differentiable cohomology gives $\operatorname{Hom}(K^{\mathrm{Ban}}(A),V)\simeq P\,R\Gamma_{\mathrm{diff}}(B\mathrm{GL}(A),V)$; for $A=\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ on a polydisc, $U_n(\mathbb{C})\backslash\mathrm{GL}_n(A)$ is contractible, so this becomes relative continuous Lie algebra cohomology, whose primitive chains reduce by Loday--Quillen and Fréchet HKR to $\widehat C_\bullet(A)\simeq\bigoplus_{p>0}(\Omega_A^{2p-\bullet}/F^{p+1})$; adjoining the $\mathfrak u$-contribution $(2\pi i)^p\mathbb{R}$ and sheafifying yields $K^{\mathrm{Ban}}(X)\simeq\bigoplus_{p\ge0}R\Gamma_D(X,\mathbb{R}(p))[2p]$ for compact complex $X$.

title: Rick Jardine
note: Rick Jardine, persistent homotopy admits a controlled homotopy theory in which Rips stability is preserved quantitatively by homotopy-theoretic gluing. Key computation: a finite metric sample $X$ defines the system $V_*(X):s\mapsto B P_s(X)$, and $d_H(X,Y)<r$ produces a homotopy interleaving $V_s(X)\to V_s(Y)\to V_{s+2r}(X)$, hence a $2r$-equivalence on every $\pi_n$; if a sectionwise cofibration $A\to B$ is an $r$-equivalence, every pushout $C\to B\cup_A C$ is a $2r$-equivalence, so for $X\subset Y$ and $X\subset W$ the comparison $V_*(W)\cup_{V_*(X)}V_*(Y)\to V_*(W\cup Y)$ is a $6r$-equivalence, giving a quantitative excision theorem for the Vietoris--Rips functor.

title: Michael Harris (joint with Wee Teck Gan and Will Sawin)
note: Michael Harris (joint with Wee Teck Gan and Will Sawin), purity and globalization force ramification of Genestier--Lafforgue parameters of supercuspidal representations over local function fields. Key computation: for $F=k((t))$, a pure supercuspidal $\pi$ compactly induced from $U=G(\mathcal{O}_F)$ is globalized over $K=k(t)$ by the Poincaré series $P_\phi(g)=\sum_{\gamma\in G(K)}\phi(\gamma g)$ with $\phi_z=\phi_\pi$ for $z\in\mathbb{G}_m(k)$, $\phi_x=1_{G(\mathcal{O}_x)}$ off $|\mathbb{P}^1(k)|$, $\phi_\infty=1_{I_{\infty,+}}$, and $\phi_0=\chi_k$, whose support gives $P_\phi(1)=1$; if $L(\pi)$ were unramified, purity would extend $L(\Pi)_\sigma$ to a punctually pure tame local system on $\mathbb{G}_m$, hence a sum of finite-order tame characters, contradicting variation of $\chi_k$, so $L(\pi)$ is ramified and, for induction from a sufficiently small compact, wildly ramified.

title: Kęstutis Česnavičius
note: Kęstutis Česnavičius, the perfectoid approach proves purity for the Brauer group and for flat cohomology with finite flat coefficients. Key computation: for a perfectoid ring $A$ and a closed $Z\subset\operatorname{Spec}(A[1/p])$ of codimension at least $2$, prismatic Dieudonné theory sends a finite locally free commutative $p$-power-order group $G$ to $M(G)=\operatorname{Ext}^1(G,\mathcal{O}_{\Prism})$ equipped with semilinear $F,V$ satisfying $FV=p$; $p$-complete arc hyperdescent reduces the resulting purity comparison to rank-one valuation rings, yielding $R\Gamma(A,G)\simeq R\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}(A[1/p])\setminus Z,G)$ and, for a regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, $H^i_{\mathfrak m}(R,G)=0$ for $i<\dim R$.

title: Yves André
note: Yves André, every finite covering of a regular scheme is an fpqc covering, equivalently every finite extension of a regular ring is dominated by a faithfully flat algebra. Key computation: for $R=\mathbb{Z}_p[[x_2,\ldots,x_n]]$ and finite reduced $R\subset S$, adjoining all $p$-power roots gives the perfectoid algebra $R_\infty=\mathbb{Z}_p[p^{1/p^\infty}][[x_2^{1/p^\infty},\ldots,x_n^{1/p^\infty}]]^{\wedge}$; after choosing $g$ with $S[1/pg]$ étale over $R[1/pg]$, perfectoid Abhyankar makes $S_\infty^\infty$ $(pg)^{1/p^\infty}$-almost finite étale over $R_\infty^\infty$, and $T=\Sigma^{-1}(\prod_{\mathbb N}S_\infty^\infty/\bigoplus_{\mathbb N}S_\infty^\infty)$ removes almostness to produce a perfectoid $S$-algebra faithfully flat over $R$.

title: Jessica Fintzen
note: Jessica Fintzen, explicitly constructed omni-supercuspidal types force arbitrary algebraic automorphic forms to be congruent modulo $p^m$ to forms supercuspidal at $p$. Key computation: when $p$ exceeds the Coxeter number of $G$, there are nested compact opens $U_{p,1}\supset U_{p,2}\supset\cdots$ and maps $\lambda_m:U_{p,m}\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{Z}/p^m\mathbb{Z}$ such that $(U_{p,m},\psi\circ\lambda_m)$ is a supercuspidal type for every nontrivial $\psi$; consequently $M(U_{p,m}U^p,\mathbb{Z}_p)/p^m\simeq M(U_{p,m}U^p,A_m)$ Hecke-equivariantly, and every automorphic representation contributing to $M(U_{p,m}U^p,A_m)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p}\mathbb{Q}_p$ has supercuspidal local factor at $p$.

title: David Vogan
note: David Vogan, real parabolic induction, cohomological induction, and weakly unipotent representations reduce the construction of large portions of the unitary dual to unitary data on Levi subgroups. Key computation: for a $\theta$-stable $P=LU$ and an $(\mathfrak l,L\cap K)$-module $\pi_L$ of infinitesimal character $\gamma=\gamma_z+\gamma_d$, Zuckerman's functors satisfy $R^i(\pi_L)=0$ for $i<s$ and $R^s(\pi_L)$ is unitary when $\pi_L$ is weakly unipotent unitary and $\gamma_z$ is weakly antidominant on coroots of $U$; for $G=\mathrm{GL}(2n)$, $L=\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$, and $\pi_L=(1\otimes|\det|^a)\otimes(1\otimes|\det|^b)$, one has $\gamma_z=[(a,\ldots,a)(b,\ldots,b)]$ and the required central condition is exactly $a-b\ge0$.

title: Mark Goresky (with Robert MacPherson
note: Mark Goresky (with Robert MacPherson, Günter Harder, and Robert Kottwitz), weighted cohomology turns Arthur's topological trace formula into a Lefschetz fixed-point formula for Hecke correspondences on arithmetic locally symmetric spaces. Key computation: the middle-weight truncation on the reductive Borel--Serre compactification satisfies $R\pi_*W^\mu H^*(X^{\mathrm{RBS}})\simeq IH^*(X^{\mathrm{BB}})\simeq H_{(2)}^*(X)$; for a hyperbolic fixed component $F$, its local term is $\operatorname{lc}(F)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(C^*\mid H^i_{\{\mathrm{expanding}\}}(U,A^\bullet))$, and summing these boundary-stratum contributions recovers Arthur's $L^2$ Lefschetz number $L(C(h))=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(q_*p^*\mid H^i_{(2)}(X;E_\rho))$ and the discrete-series character factor.

title: Guozhen Wang (joint with Ruochuan Liu)
note: Guozhen Wang (joint with Ruochuan Liu), prismatic descent computes the mod-$p$ topological cyclic homology of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ from a perfectoid resolution. Key computation: for $R=\mathbb{Z}_p[p^{1/p^\infty}]^{\wedge}$, the descent Hopf algebroid gives $E_2^{*,*,*}=\mathbb{F}_p[f,g,\sigma^{\pm1}]/(g^2)$, and with $\psi(k)=(p^k-1)/(p-1)$ its Tate differentials are $d_{p\psi(k)}(f^{p^{k-1}})=g f^{p^{k-1}+\psi(k)-1}$; the survivors recover $(\mathrm{TC}/p)_*(\mathbb{Z}_p)$ as a free $\mathbb{F}_p[v_1]$-module on $\{1,\gamma,a_0\gamma,a_m\mid0\le m\le p-1\}$, in stems $0,-1,2p-2$, and $2p-2m-1$ respectively.

title: Neil Strickland
note: Neil Strickland, Morava $K$-theories classify the thick subcategories of finite spectra and organize stable homotopy into chromatic layers. Key computation: a finite $p$-local spectrum $X$ has type $n$ when $K(p,n)_*(X)\ne0$ but $K(p,m)_*(X)=0$ for $m<n$, defining $\mathcal{F}(p,n)$; every thick subcategory is one of the $\mathcal{F}(p,n)$, while periodicity supplies $v:\Sigma^dX\to X$ inducing an isomorphism on $K(p,n)_*(X)$, and chromatic convergence decomposes $\pi_*X$ into layers controlled by $K(p,n)$ with eventual periods $2(p^n-1)p^k$.

title: Gautier Ponsinet
note: Gautier Ponsinet, universal norms of de Rham representations over perfectoid extensions are controlled by the positive Hodge--Tate part via the Fargues--Fontaine curve. Key computation: if $V$ is de Rham with Hodge--Tate weights at most $1$ and $V_0\subset V$ is minimal such that $V/V_0$ has weights at most $0$, then for $T_0=T\cap V_0$ and perfectoid $\widehat L$, $H_e^1(L,V/T)=\operatorname{Im}(H^1(L,V_0/T_0)\to H^1(L,V/T))$; for an abelian variety, $\widetilde{\widehat A}=\varprojlim_{[p]}\widehat A\simeq\Gamma(X_{FF},\mathcal{E}(\widetilde{\widehat A}))$ with all Harder--Narasimhan slopes positive, so the bundle classification gives $H^1(L,\widetilde{\widehat A})=0$ and recovers the Coates--Greenberg description of the Kummer image.

title: Christian Sattler and David Wärn
note: Christian Sattler and David Wärn, a short proposition-valued axiom system inside homotopy type theory reconstructs the basic calculus of univalent $\infty$-categories. Key computation: defining $[0]=\mathbf{1}$ and $[n+1]=\operatorname{Fun}([n],I)$, the Segal pushout $[2]\simeq I\amalg_{\mathbf{1}}I$ makes $\operatorname{Map}([2],C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(I,C)\times_{\operatorname{Ob}(C)}\operatorname{Map}(I,C)$ and hence defines composition; inductively $[n]$ is the colimit of its spine, giving $\operatorname{Map}([n],C)\simeq\sum_{a:\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)\to\operatorname{Ob}(C)}\prod_{i:\operatorname{Fin}(n)}C(a_i,a_{i+1})$, while the Rezk axiom identifies $(x\simeq y)\simeq(x=y)$.

title: Gabriele Vezzosi
note: Gabriele Vezzosi, derived algebraic geometry realizes the reduced obstruction theory for stable maps to a K3 surface as the cotangent complex of a quasi-smooth derived Deligne--Mumford stack. Key computation: for a stable map $f:C\to S$, the standard obstruction space fits into $H^1(C,T_C)\to H^1(C,f^*T_S)\to\operatorname{Obs}_f\to0$, and the symplectic identification $T_S\simeq\Omega_S^1$ followed by $df$ gives a surjection $a:\operatorname{Obs}_f\to H^1(C,\omega_C)\simeq\mathbb{C}$, forcing $[\overline{M}_g(S;\beta)]_{\mathrm{std}}^{\mathrm{vir}}=0$; removing this factor produces a quasi-smooth $R\overline{M}_g^{\mathrm{red}}(S;\beta)$ with obstruction space $\ker a$ and the nontrivial reduced virtual class.

title: Jared Weinstein
note: Jared Weinstein, diamonds turn analytic adic spaces over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ into pro-étale sheaves and identify perfectoid spaces over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ with characteristic-$p$ perfectoid spaces over the diamond $\operatorname{Spd}\mathbb{Q}_p$. Key computation: $\operatorname{Spd}\mathbb{Q}_p=(\operatorname{Spd}\mathbb{Q}_p^{\mathrm{cycl}})/\mathbb{Z}_p^*$ and $(\operatorname{Spd}\mathbb{Q}_p)(S)=\{S^\sharp\to\operatorname{Spa}\mathbb{Q}_p:(S^\sharp)^\flat\simeq S\}$; for $R$ a $\mathbb{Q}_p$-vector space the associated diamond $\widetilde H_C^\diamond(R)=H^0(X_{R^\flat},\mathcal O(1))$ fits into $0\to\mathbb{Q}_p(1)\to\widetilde H_C^\diamond\to\mathbb A_C^{1,\diamond}\to0$, and the construction yields $\{\text{perfectoid spaces}/\mathbb{Q}_p\}\simeq\{X/\mathbb F_p\text{ perfectoid}:X\to\operatorname{Spd}\mathbb{Q}_p\}$.

title: Charles Rezk
note: Charles Rezk, height-$2$ Morava $E$-theory at $p=2$ gives an explicit twisted bialgebra of power operations, making $\pi_0$ of every $K(2)$-local commutative $E$-algebra an amplified $\Gamma$-ring. Key computation: for $E_0=\mathbb Z_2[[a]]$, additive operations $Q_0,Q_1,Q_2$ satisfy $Q_1Q_0=2Q_2Q_1-2Q_0Q_2$, $Q_2Q_0=Q_0Q_1+aQ_0Q_2-2Q_1Q_2$, and $Q_0(x)=x^2+2\theta(x)$; their Cartan formulas are encoded by $\Delta(Q_0)=Q_0\otimes Q_0+2Q_1\otimes Q_2+2Q_2\otimes Q_1$ and analogous displayed formulas for $\Delta(Q_1),\Delta(Q_2)$, while $\Gamma$ has left $\mathbb Z_2[[a]]$-basis $Q_0^iQ_{j_1}\cdots Q_{j_r}$ with $j_k\in\{1,2\}$, yielding $\pi_0L_{K(2)}\mathbb P_E(E)\simeq \widehat F_{(2,a)}$ for the free amplified $\Gamma$-ring $F$.

title: Agnès Beaudry
note: Agnès Beaudry, the extended Morava stabilizer group realizes the $K(n)$-local sphere as homotopy fixed points of Morava $E$-theory and turns the local Adams--Novikov spectral sequence into continuous group cohomology. Key computation: Lubin--Tate deformation theory gives $(E_n)_0=\mathbb Z_{p^n}[[u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}]]$ representing deformations of the height-$n$ Honda formal group and $\mathbb G_n=\{(f,i):i\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_{p^n}/\mathbb F_p),\ f:i^*\Gamma_n\xrightarrow\sim\Gamma_n\}$; Goerss--Hopkins--Miller lifts its action to $E_n$, and $(E_n)_*E_n\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_c(\mathbb G_n,(E_n)_*)$ promotes to $L_{K(n)}E_n^{\bullet+1}\simeq F_c((\mathbb G_n)^{\bullet+},E_n)$, hence $L_{K(n)}S^0\simeq E_n^{h\mathbb G_n}$ with $H_c^*(\mathbb G_n,(E_n)_*)\Longrightarrow\pi_*L_{K(n)}S^0$.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, Koszul cdgas retain relations among defining equations and make derived intersections quasi-smooth with the expected virtual dimension, recovering Bézout counts without transversality. Key computation: for $p_1,\ldots,p_n\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$, the cdga $A^*=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_m;y_1,\ldots,y_n]$ with $|y_i|=-1$ and $dy_i=p_i$ has $H^0(A^*)=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/(p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ but its $H^{-1}$ distinguishes dependent presentations such as $(x^2,y^2)$ and $(x^2,y^2,x^2+y^2)$; thus $\operatorname{Spec}A^*$ has $\operatorname{vdim}=m-n$, and for plane curves $C,D\subset\mathbb{CP}^2$ of degrees $m,n$, the derived intersection $C\times^R_{\mathbb{CP}^2}D$ is proper quasi-smooth of virtual dimension $0$ with $[C\times^R_{\mathbb{CP}^2}D]^{\mathrm{virt}}=mn$ even when the classical intersection has dimension $1$.

title: Giovanni Landi
note: Giovanni Landi, Connes's reconstruction theorem characterizes compact oriented spin$^c$ manifolds spectrally, with the Dirac operator recovering dimension, distance, and measure from the commutative algebra. Key computation: an $n$-dimensional spectral triple has resolvent singular values $\mu_k(|D|)\sim2\pi\bigl(k/(\Omega_n\operatorname{vol}M)\bigr)^{1/n}$ and Connes's distance formula $d(p,q)=\sup\{|f(p)-f(q)|:f\in C^\infty(M),\ \|[D,f]\|\le1\}$, while integration is the Dixmier trace $\int_M f\,d\mu_g\sim\mathop{\rlap{-}\!\int}f|D|^{-n}$; imposing the first-order and orientability relations together with the spectral conditions and multiplicity $2^{n/2}$ reconstructs $A=C^\infty(M)$ and $D$ as a Dirac operator, whereas the noncommutative example $(A(SU_q(2)),H,D)$ is regular, $3^+$-summable, and has dimension spectrum $\{1,2,3\}$ and $KO$-dimension $3$.

title: Hal Schenck (joint with R
note:
Hal Schenck (joint with R. Di Gennaro, G. Ilardi, R. M. Miró-Roig, and J. Vallès), finite eigenschemes classify free plane curves annihilated by a fixed derivation and control singular members of pencils. Key computation: for $\delta=P_1\partial_x+P_2\partial_y+P_3\partial_z$ of degree $a$ with finite eigenscheme $\Gamma_\delta$ cut out by the $2	imes2$ minors of $ egin{psmallmatrix}x&P_1\y&P_2\z&P_3\end{psmallmatrix}$, the resolution $0	o\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^2}(-1)\oplus\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^2}(-a)	o\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^2}^3	o\mathcal J_{\Gamma_\delta}(a+1)	o0$ gives $\operatorname{length}(\Gamma_\delta)=1+a+a^2$; if $f\in R_d$, $d\ge a+1$, and $\delta(f)=0$, then $V(f)$ is free with exponents $(a,d-a-1)$ exactly when $f\in I_{\Gamma_\delta}$, while for a pencil generated by reduced $f\in R_n,g\in R_m$, the canonical derivation $\delta_{f,g}=\det(
abla f,
abla g,
abla)$ bounds singular members away from the base locus by $(n-1)^2+(n-1)(m-1)+(m-1)^2$.

title: Nathan Pagliaroli (joint with Hamed Hessam
note: Nathan Pagliaroli (joint with Hamed Hessam, Masoud Khalkhali, and Luuk Verhoeven), quartic random fuzzy spectral triples reduce to explicit bi-tracial matrix models whose equilibrium measure computes a one-cut/two-cut spectral phase transition and identifies a double-scaling gravity class. Key computation: for the type $(1,0)$ triple $(M_N(\mathbb C),M_N(\mathbb C),D=\{H,\cdot\})$, $\int e^{-g\operatorname{Tr}D^2-\operatorname{Tr}D^4}\,dD$ becomes $\int e^{-[2Ng\operatorname{Tr}H^2+2g(\operatorname{Tr}H)^2+2N\operatorname{Tr}H^4+8\operatorname{Tr}H\operatorname{Tr}H^3+6(\operatorname{Tr}H^2)^2]}\,dH$; the one-cut density $\Psi(x)=\pi^{-1}(-4a^2+\tfrac1{2a^2}+4x^2)\sqrt{4a^2-x^2}_+$ reaches zero at $a_c=1/\sqrt[4]{8}$, giving $g_c=-4\sqrt2$, after which $\Psi(x)=\tfrac2\pi|x|\sqrt{(x^2-a^2)(b^2-x^2)}_+$ has two-cut support; the double-scaling limit is the $(3,2)$ pure-gravity minimal model.

title: Matthew Kennedy (joint results with Eli Shamovich and with Laurent Marcoux and Mikael…
note: Matthew Kennedy (joint results with Eli Shamovich and with Laurent Marcoux and Mikael Rørdam Skoufranis), noncommutative Choquet theory classifies matrix-convex simplices and turns majorization of operator tuples into existence of a doubly stochastic completely positive map. Key computation: a compact noncommutative convex set $K$ is an nc simplex precisely when each $x\in K$ has a unique maximal representing nc state, equivalently $A(K)^{**}$ is a von Neumann algebra; the nc Choquet order is the dilation order $\mu\prec_{\mathrm{nc}}\nu$ iff a Stinespring representation satisfies $\pi_\nu|_{A(K)}=\begin{psmallmatrix}\pi_\mu|_{A(K)}&*\\ *&*\end{psmallmatrix}$. Consequently, for self-adjoint tuples $a=(a_i),b=(b_i)$ in a finite von Neumann algebra $(M,\tau)$, the inequalities $f(a)\le f(b)$ for every continuous convex nc function $f$ are equivalent to $a_i=\varphi(b_i)$ for all $i$ under one normal unital completely positive trace-preserving map $\varphi:M\to M$.

title: Markus J
note: Markus J. Pflaum (joint with Hessel Posthuma and Xiang Tang), Hochschild homology of a proper Lie-groupoid convolution algebra localizes to its orbit space and, for compact actions, is computed from differential forms on fixed-point loci and the inertia space. Key computation: for the convolution sheaf $\mathcal A$ on $X=M/G$, diagonal cutoff chain maps $\Psi_{k,\varepsilon}(x_0,\ldots,x_k)=\prod_{j=0}^k\rho_\varepsilon(d^2(x_j,x_{j+1}))$ admit homotopies $bH_{k,\varepsilon}+H_{k-1,\varepsilon}b=1-\Psi_\varepsilon$, proving $HH_*(\mathcal A(X))\simeq\Gamma(X;\mathcal{HH}_*(\mathcal A))$; each stalk reduces to $C^\infty(G_x\ltimes N_x\mathcal O)$, and the twisted Connes--HKR complex $(\Omega^*(V),\iota_{Y_h})$ for $Y_h(v)=v-hv$ is quasi-isomorphic via restriction and projection to $(\Omega^*(V^h),0)$, hence $H_k(C^\infty(V),{}_hC^\infty(V))\simeq\Omega^k(V^h)$ and verifies Brylinski's inertia-form model for circle actions.

title: Jamie Mingo
note: Jamie Mingo, noncrossing-partition cumulants characterize free independence and convert the moment sequence of a noncommutative random variable into Voiculescu's compositional-transform equation. Key computation: Möbius inversion on $NC(n)$ gives $\kappa_n(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=\sum_{\pi\in NC(n)}\mu_{NC(n)}(\pi,1_n)\varphi_\pi(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ and $\varphi(a_1\cdots a_n)=\sum_{\pi\in NC(n)}\kappa_\pi(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$; unital subalgebras $A_1,\ldots,A_s$ are freely independent iff every mixed cumulant vanishes, namely $\kappa_n(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=0$ whenever $a_i\in A_{j_i}$ and $\ker(j)\ne1_n$. Decomposing a noncrossing partition by the block containing $1$ yields $m_n=\sum_{s=1}^n\kappa_s\sum_{i_1+\cdots+i_s+s=n}m_{i_1}\cdots m_{i_s}$, hence $C(zM(z))=M(z)$ and $R(z)=G^{\langle-1\rangle}(z)-z^{-1}$.

title: Andrew J
note: Andrew J. Blumberg, trace methods identify topological Hochschild homology by the Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel norm and recover $TR$ and $TC$ from curves in algebraic $K$-theory. Key computation: for a ring spectrum $R$, the slides model $\mathrm{THH}(R)$ as $N_e^{S^1}R$ and state that the equivariant homotopy type of $\mathrm{THH}$ of a Thom spectrum is again an equivariant Thom spectrum; the cyclotomic restriction and Frobenius maps assemble $\widetilde K(R[x]/x^n)$ over the indexing category $I$, and the completed limits $\varprojlim_I\Omega\widetilde K(R[x]/x^n)$ recover $\mathrm{TR}(R)$ and $\mathrm{TC}(R)$, while $K\operatorname{End}(\mathcal C)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Mot}}(S[t],\mathcal C)$ identifies the trace motivically.

title: Maria Yakerson
note: Maria Yakerson, finite-flat transfers give a universal framed model for connective motivic algebraic $K$-theory and a Hilbert-scheme presentation over a perfect field. Key computation: the slides identify the motivic spectrum $\mathrm{kgl}$ with the framed suspension spectrum generated by the presheaf $\mathrm{Vect}$ of vector bundles, using the $\mathbb A^1$-equivalence obtained from the Rees algebra of the canonical filtration on a finite flat algebra; group completion then turns the forgetful map from finite-flat Hilbert schemes to $\mathrm{Vect}$ into an $\mathbb A^1$-equivalence, producing $\Omega_T^\infty\mathrm{kgl}\simeq L_{\mathrm{mot}}\operatorname{Hilb}^{\mathrm{fl}}(\mathbb A^\infty)$.

title: Maxence Mayrand (joint with Peter Crooks)
note: Maxence Mayrand (joint with Peter Crooks), shifted symplectic geometry proves the regular Moore--Tachikawa construction of a two-dimensional TQFT from a complex semisimple group. Key computation: composition of $1$-shifted Lagrangian correspondences is the derived fibre product $L_1\times_{G_2}L_2$, and Hamiltonian composition is symplectic reduction $(M\times N)//H$; Kostant's slice $S\subset\mathfrak g^*_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and abelian regular stabilizers give a Morita equivalence $T^*G|_{\mathfrak g^*_{\mathrm{reg}}}\simeq T^*G|_S$, so the resulting abelian quasi-symplectic groupoid is a commutative Frobenius object and hence defines $\eta_G:\operatorname{Cob}_2\to\mathrm{Weinstein}^{1\text{-}\mathrm{symp}}$.

title: Iva Halacheva
note: Iva Halacheva, Rickard complexes in categorical $\mathfrak g$-representations yield perverse equivalences whose action on simple objects is the crystal cactus-group action. Key computation: for a categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action, $\Theta_n=(\cdots\to E^{(n+2)}F^{(2)}\to E^{(n+1)}F^{(1)}\to E^{(n)})$ induces $D^b(\mathcal C_{-n})\simeq D^b(\mathcal C_n)$ and decategorifies to $s|_{V_{-n}}=\sum_k(-1)^ke^{(n+k)}f^{(k)}$; composing these complexes along a reduced word for $w_0^J$ gives bijections $\theta_J$ on $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ satisfying $\theta_J^2=1$, $\theta_J\theta_K=\theta_K\theta_J$, and $\theta_J\theta_K=\theta_{J^*(K)}\theta_J$, hence $c_J\mapsto\theta_J$ realizes the cactus group and agrees with Schützenberger involutions on crystals.

title: Michael Rosbotham (joint with Martin Mathieu)
note: Michael Rosbotham (joint with Martin Mathieu), relative homological algebra classifies unital operator algebras of completely bounded global dimension zero as finite direct sums of full matrix algebras. Key computation: the forgetful functor $F:\operatorname{OMod}_A^\infty\to\operatorname{Op}^\infty$ defines the exact structure $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{rel}}=\{(\mu,\pi)\in\mathcal E_{\max}:(F\mu,F\pi)\in\mathcal E_{\min}\}$; $E$ is relatively projective exactly when there are completely bounded $A$-module maps $s:E\to E\otimes_hA$ and $r:E\otimes_hA\to E$ with $rs=\operatorname{id}_E$, so all operator $A$-modules are relatively projective iff $A$ is classically semisimple, and Artin--Wedderburn plus Gelfand--Mazur yields $d_{gcb}(A)=0\Longleftrightarrow A\cong\bigoplus_iM_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$.

title: Emily Riehl
note: Emily Riehl, univalent foundations encode higher-categorical composition by contractibility and support a machine computation of $\pi_4(S^3)$. Key computation: univalence makes $\operatorname{id\text{-}to\text{-}equiv}:(A=_{\mathcal U}B)\to(A\simeq B)$ an equivalence, while the composite space $\operatorname{Comp}(f,g)$ of two paths is a pullback of $\operatorname{Map}(\Delta,X)\to\operatorname{Map}(\Lambda,X)$ and is contractible because $D^n\times\Delta$ deformation-retracts onto $S^{n-1}\times\Delta\cup_{S^{n-1}\times\Lambda}D^n\times\Lambda$; this contractible-choice principle supplies composition in synthetic $\infty$-categories, and the constructive Hopf-fibration/Freudenthal/Blakers--Massey calculation normalizes in Cubical Agda to the Brunerie number $n=-2$, hence $\pi_4(S^3)\cong\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$.

title: Pádraig Daly
note: Pádraig Daly, operator-system methods classify quantum superchannels, prove every channel-space supermap extends to a superchannel, and characterize extreme constrained completely positive extensions. Key computation: the Choi map identifies $S_{\mathrm{CPTP}}(d,r)$ completely order isomorphically with $S(d,r)=\{(P_{ij}):\operatorname{Tr}P_{ii}=\operatorname{Tr}P_{jj},\ \operatorname{Tr}P_{ij}=0\ (i\ne j)\}$; a CPTP-preserving $\Gamma$ is a quantum superchannel exactly when the induced $\widetilde\Gamma:S(d_1,r_1)\to S(d_2,r_2)$ is completely positive, so Arveson's extension theorem and Choi's theorem produce $S(\varphi)=\psi_{\mathrm{post}}\circ(\operatorname{id}_e\otimes\varphi)\circ\psi_{\mathrm{pre}}$, with minimal $e=\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Tr}_{r_1}\operatorname{Tr}_{r_2}C_{\widetilde S})$; two extensions induce the same action precisely subject to $\operatorname{Tr}_{d_1}(C_{\widetilde S_1}-C_{\widetilde S_2})=0$.

title: Reyer Sjamaar (joint work with Florian Dorsch
note: Reyer Sjamaar (joint work with Florian Dorsch, Miguel Cueca, and Chenchang Zhu), derived higher Lie groupoids encode singular symplectic reduction as a shifted symplectic groupoid Morita equivalent to a derived Lagrangian intersection. Key computation: a derived manifold $\mathcal M=(M,E_\bullet,X_\bullet)$ has tangent complex $T_mM\to E_{1,m}\to\cdots$, and weak equivalences are bijective on classical loci and quasi-isomorphisms on these complexes; for a Hamiltonian $G$-manifold $(M,\omega,\mu)$, the derived action groupoid $G\times(\mathfrak g^*\times M)\rightrightarrows(\mathfrak g^*\times M)$ has tangent total complex $0\to\mathfrak g\to T_mM\to\mathfrak g^*\to0$, while $(\omega,\mu)$ is closed in the de Rham triple complex because $d\omega=0$ and $\delta\omega=d\mu$, and its induced pairing is a quasi-isomorphism $T\simeq T^\vee$, giving the $0$-shifted symplectic derived quotient $M//G$.

title: Adam Humeniuk
note: Adam Humeniuk, the $C^*$-covers of a nonselfadjoint operator algebra form a complete lattice, and explicit constructions separate five natural notions of equality of cover data. Key computation: ordering covers by $(C,\iota)\geq(D,\eta)$ when a surjective $*$-homomorphism $C\twoheadrightarrow D$ intertwines $\iota$ and $\eta$ makes $C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(A)$ a complete lattice with extrema $C^*_{\max}(A)$ and $C^*_{\mathrm{env}}(A)$; the formulas $C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(A\oplus B)\cong C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(A)\times C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(B)$ and, for nuclear simple $B$, $C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(A\otimes B)\cong C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(A)\otimes B$ yield examples such as $T_2$ and $T_2\otimes M_2\cong M_2(T_2)$ that are lattice-isomorphic but not lattice-intertwined, proving that isomorphism, intertwining, lattice $*$-isomorphism, lattice isomorphism, and cover equivalence are genuinely distinct.

title: Michael Brannan (joint with Kari Eifler
note: Michael Brannan (joint with Kari Eifler, Christian Voigt, and Moritz Weber), quantum graphs admit universal quantum Cuntz--Krieger algebras that recover the classical construction for commutative vertex algebras and exhibit new nonnuclear examples. Key computation: for $\mathcal G=(B,\psi,A)$ with $B=\bigoplus_{k=1}^mM_{n(k)}(\mathbb C)$, writing $S^{(k)}=(\dim B/n(k))[S(e_{ij}^{(k)})]$ turns the defining relation $\mu(1\otimes\mu)(S\otimes S^*\otimes S)(1\otimes m^*)m^*=S$ into $S^{(k)}S^{(k)*}S^{(k)}=S^{(k)}$, while $\mu(S^*\otimes S)m^*=\mu(S\otimes S^*)m^*A$ becomes $S^{(k)*}S^{(k)}=(S^{(1)}S^{(1)*},\ldots,S^{(m)}S^{(m)*})\widetilde A$; these relations define $\mathcal O_{\mathcal G}$, give $\mathcal O_{\mathcal G}$ equal to the usual Cuntz--Krieger algebra when $B$ is abelian, and for the complete quantum graph yield the explicit quotient $\mathcal O_{K(M_n)}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_{n^2}$ by $S_{ij}\mapsto n^{-1/2}\widehat S_{ij}$.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, global quotient stacks form a $(2,1)$-category in which classifying stacks retain automorphisms of principal bundles and $2$-fibre products differ essentially from fibre products in the homotopy category. Key computation: morphisms $U\to[*/\Gamma]$ classify principal $\Gamma$-bundles $P\to U$, and the fibre product of $[U/\Gamma]\to[W/K]\leftarrow[V/\Delta]$ is $[\{(u,v,k):f(u)=kg(v)\}/(\Gamma\times\Delta)]$ with $(\gamma,\delta)(u,v,k)=(\gamma u,\delta v,\rho(\gamma)k\sigma(\delta)^{-1})$; in particular $*\times_{[*/\Gamma]}*\simeq\Gamma$, so pulling back the tautological $*\to[*/\Gamma]$ along the classifying map recovers $P\to U$.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, coherent sheaves on $\mathbb{CP}^1$ are classified by line bundles and finite-length skyscraper sheaves, and torsion-free sheaves compactify moduli of vector bundles by admitting singular limits. Key computation: the exact sequence $0\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}\xrightarrow{s^{\otimes k}}\mathcal O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}(k)\to\mathcal O_{[x,y]}^{(k)}\to0$ constructs the length-$k$ torsion summands, and every $E\in\operatorname{coh}(\mathbb{CP}^1)$ decomposes uniquely as a finite direct sum of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}(n)$ and $\mathcal O_{[x,y]}^{(k)}$; on $\mathbb{CP}^2$, the cokernel of $(y,z,\delta\operatorname{id}):\mathcal O\to\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}\oplus\mathcal O$ is $\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$ for $\delta\ne0$ but specializes at $\delta=0$ to $(I_{[1,0,0]}\otimes\mathcal O(2))\oplus\mathcal O$, an explicit non-locally-free torsion-free limit.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, Dwyer--Kan hammock localization upgrades inversion of weak equivalences from an ordinary homotopy category to a simplicial model for the associated $\infty$-category, while horn filling distinguishes categories, groupoids, and quasicategories. Key computation: for a model category $\mathcal M$, the mapping simplicial set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{DK}}(X,Y)$ is built from rows of zigzags $X\leftarrow^{\sim}K_1\leftarrow^{\sim}L_1\to K_2\leftarrow^{\sim}\cdots\to Y$, and $\pi_0\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{DK}}(X,Y)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M[W^{-1}]}(X,Y)$; moreover a simplicial set is $N(\mathcal C)$ exactly when every inner horn has a unique filler, and $N(\mathcal C)$ is Kan exactly when $\mathcal C$ is a groupoid, identifying Kan complexes as models for $\infty$-groupoids and weak Kan complexes as quasicategories.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, PTVV shifted symplectic structures turn Calabi--Yau moduli into explicit local critical-locus geometry and lower the shift under derived Lagrangian intersection. Key computation: for the derived moduli stack $\mathcal M$ of coherent complexes on a Calabi--Yau $m$-fold, $h^i(T_{\mathcal M}|_E)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}(E,E)$ and Serre duality $\operatorname{Ext}^i(E,E)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{m-i}(E,E)^*$ induce the nondegenerate quasi-isomorphism $T_{\mathcal M}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\mathcal M}[2-m]$, hence a $(2-m)$-shifted symplectic form; if $L,M\to(X,\omega_k)$ are Lagrangian then $L\times_XM$ is $(k-1)$-shifted symplectic, and for $k=-1$ the shifted Darboux theorem gives $(X,\omega)\simeq\operatorname{Crit}(H:U\to\mathbb A^1)$ Zariski locally, so Calabi--Yau $3$-fold sheaf moduli are locally classical critical loci.

title: Jared Weinstein
note: Jared Weinstein, Faltings's two-towers theorem identifies the Lubin--Tate and Drinfeld towers as quotient $v$-stacks and converts Morava-stabilizer cohomology into $p$-adic Lie-group cohomology. Key computation: the isomorphism $[\mathrm{LT}_{n,\eta}^{\diamond}/\mathbb G_n]\cong[\mathcal H_{n-1}^{\diamond}/\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb Z_p)]$ arises because a height-$n$, dimension-$1$ $p$-divisible group $G/\mathcal O_C$ has Hodge--Tate sequence $0\to\operatorname{Lie}G\otimes C(1)\to T_pG\otimes C\to(\operatorname{Lie}G^*)^*\otimes C\to0$, determining a line in $T_pG\otimes C$, with the formal-group locus exactly Drinfeld's $\mathcal H_{n-1}$; taking $\mathcal O^+$-cohomology yields $H^*(\mathbb G_n,W(\mathbb F_p))\to H^*(\mathbb G_n,W(\mathbb F_p)[[u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}]])$ as an isomorphism after inverting $p$ and $H^*(\mathbb G_n,E_n^0)[1/p]\cong\mathbb Q_p[x_1,x_3,\ldots,x_{2n-1}]$ with $|x_i|=i$.

title: Dihua Jiang
note: Dihua Jiang, consecutive local descents of enhanced Langlands parameters classify the arithmetic wavefront set of generic representations of classical groups by rational nilpotent orbits. Key computation: local Gan--Gross--Prasad gives $\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{M_{\ell,X}}(J_X(V_\pi)\otimes\widehat\sigma^\vee,1)=1$ exactly when the component-group characters satisfy $(\chi,\chi')=(\chi^z_{\phi,\varphi},\chi^z_{\varphi,\phi})$; defining $D_\ell(\phi,\chi)=\bigcup_{z\in F^\times/F^{\times2}}D_\ell^z(\phi,\chi)$ and $\ell_0=\max\{\ell:D_\ell(\phi,\chi)\ne\varnothing\}$, first descent is discrete and $\ell_0(\pi)=\ell_0(\phi,\chi)$, so iteration produces signed Young-tableau data $(\ell_j,q(\ell_j))$ and a canonical orbit set $\mathrm{WF}_{\mathrm{ari}}(\pi)$; over $\mathbb R$, if $S_\phi\ne1$ then $\mathrm{WF}_{\mathrm{ari}}(\pi)_{\max}=\{\mathcal O_a(\phi,\chi)\}$, a unique rational nilpotent orbit determining a stable orbit.

title: Wee Teck Gan
note: Wee Teck Gan, the endoscopic classification of the metaplectic group $\operatorname{Mp}_{2n}$ decomposes its discrete automorphic spectrum into packets indexed by elliptic Arthur parameters, with multiplicities controlled by component-group characters and central epsilon factors. Key computation: for $\Psi=\boxplus_i\Pi_i\boxtimes S_{d_i}$ the local packet is $\widetilde\Pi_{\Psi_v,\psi_v}=\bigoplus_{\eta_v\in\operatorname{Irr}(S_{\Psi_v})}\eta_v\otimes\widetilde\pi_{\eta_v}$ and $\widetilde A_{n,\mathrm{disc}}=\bigoplus_\Psi\widetilde A_{\Psi,\psi}$ with $\widetilde A_{\Psi,\psi}=\langle\widetilde\epsilon_\Psi,\Delta^*(\widetilde\Pi_{\Psi,\psi})\rangle_{S_\Psi}$, where $\widetilde\epsilon_\Psi=\epsilon_\Psi\widetilde\eta_\Psi$ and $\widetilde\eta_\Psi(e_i)=\epsilon(1/2,\Pi_i)$ for symplectic $\Pi_i$ and $1$ for orthogonal $\Pi_i$; locally, endoscopic transfer satisfies $t_{a,b}^*(\Theta_\Psi)=\epsilon(1/2,\Psi_b)\sum_\eta\eta(s_{a,b})\Theta_{\widetilde\pi_\eta}$ for $s_{a,b}=(1_{2a},-1_{2b})$.

title: Yiannis Sakellaridis (joint with Chen Wan)
note: Yiannis Sakellaridis (joint with Chen Wan), comparison of the Jacquet--Zagier and Kuznetsov trace formulas separates the residual spectrum of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ into boundary terms indexed by generic length. Key computation: after partially compactifying Whittaker test functions there is an isomorphism $U:\mathcal S(G/G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal S^+((N,\psi)\backslash G/(N,\psi))$ pulling stable characters back to relative characters and satisfying $\mathrm{STF}(f)=\mathrm{KTF}(Uf)+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}B_j(f)$; the Kuznetsov main term has spectral expansion over generic automorphic representations, whereas $B_j$ has expansion over representations of generic length $n-j$, and meromorphic comparison in a parameter $s$ pairs the divergence of the naive trace formula with the pole of $L(\pi,\operatorname{Ad},s)$, so taking $\operatorname{Res}_{s=1}$ yields the noninvariant trace-formula identity with all residual boundary contributions separated.

title: Bill Casselman
note: Bill Casselman, the inverse Satake transform gives an explicit basic Schwartz function for every irreducible finite-dimensional representation of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}_2$, reducing the construction to symmetric-power multiplicities and vector partition functions. Key computation: for $F_{m,n}=\mathbf1_{K\varpi^{(m,n)}K}$, $\mathcal S^{-1}(\det^nq^{(m-n)/2}\chi_{m-n})=\Phi_{m,n}=\sum_{i:m-i\ge n+i}F_{m-i,n+i}$, while $\det(I-At)^{-1}=\sum_{m\ge0}\operatorname{tr}S^m(A)t^m$ and $S^m(\sigma_k)=\sum_{i\le km/2}\delta_{km}(i)\det^i\sigma_{km-2i}$ imply that the $L$-function's basic function is $\sum_{i\le km/2}q^i\delta_{km}(i)\Phi_{km-i,i}$; writing the weight multiplicity piecewise as $\omega_{km}(n)=\sum_{j=0}^i(-1)^jD_{\alpha_j}(n-m_j)$ on $m_i\le n\le m_{i+1}$ proves it is quasi-polynomial on each Sturmfels cone and yields the displayed Sylvester asymptotics for $\omega_{km}$ and $\delta_{km}$.

title: Malors Espinosa (joint with Melissa Emory
note: Malors Espinosa (joint with Melissa Emory, Debanjana Kundu, and Tian An Wong), interpolation and Poisson summation isolate the trivial and special-representation traces inside the regular elliptic trace formula for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over a totally real number field. Key computation: contributing elliptic classes are exactly $(\tau,u)\in\mathcal O_K\times\mathcal O_K^\times$ with $\tau^2-4u\epsilon$ nonsquare, and $(\tau^2-4u\epsilon)=\mathfrak S_\gamma^2\Delta_\gamma$ defines $O(z,\gamma)=N(\mathfrak S_\gamma)^z\sum_{\mathfrak d\mid\mathfrak S_\gamma}N(\mathfrak d)^{1-2z}\prod_{\mathfrak q\mid\mathfrak d'}(1-\chi_\gamma(\mathfrak q)N(\mathfrak q)^{-z})$; then $O(1,\gamma)=\prod_{\mathfrak q}O(\gamma,f_\mathfrak q)$ and $\Lambda(z,\chi_\gamma)O(z,\gamma)=\Lambda(1-z,\chi_\gamma)O(1-z,\gamma)$, while Poisson summation gives $\operatorname{Tr}(1(f))=p^{-k/2}(1-p^{-(k+1)})(1-p^{-1})^{-1}\sum_\pm\int_{\mathbb R^{2n-1}}\theta_\pm(x,y)\,dx\,dy$ and identifies the second residue as $-2$ times the special-representation trace.

title: Andrew Dean (joint with Luis Santiago)
note: Andrew Dean (joint with Luis Santiago), triples of real, complexified, and quaternionified Cuntz semigroups classify unital real AI algebras and their homomorphisms up to approximate unitary equivalence. Key computation: $\operatorname{Inv}(A)$ is the diagram $(\operatorname{Cu}(A),[1])\to(\operatorname{Cu}(A\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C),[1])\to(\operatorname{Cu}(A\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb H),[1])$; every morphism $\eta=(\eta_r,\eta_c,\eta_h):\operatorname{Inv}(A)\to\operatorname{Inv}(B)$ is realized by a unital $*$-homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ with $(\operatorname{Cu}(\varphi),\operatorname{Cu}(\varphi\otimes_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C}),\operatorname{Cu}(\varphi\otimes_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb H}))=(\eta_r,\eta_c,\eta_h)$, and equality $\operatorname{Inv}(\varphi)=\operatorname{Inv}(\psi)$ implies $\varphi\sim_{\mathrm{a.u.}}\psi$.

title: Joachim Zacharias (joint with Joan Bosa
note: Joachim Zacharias (joint with Joan Bosa, Francesc Perera, and Jianchao Wu), almost elementary actions have $\mathcal Z$-stable crossed products and unify almost finite dynamics with $\mathcal Z$-stability of simple nuclear algebras. Key computation: a noncommutative tower is a c.p.c. order-zero map $\lambda:M_n\otimes C(S)\to A$ satisfying $\lambda(\,\cdot\,\otimes\delta_g)=\alpha_{gh^{-1}}\lambda(\,\cdot\,\otimes\delta_h)$; castles approximating finite sets with $1-\lambda(h)\precsim_G b$ and $\|h-g\cdot h\|<\varepsilon$ define almost elementariness, for which $\alpha:G\curvearrowright A\Rightarrow A\rtimes_\alpha G$ is almost elementary and hence $\mathcal Z$-stable, while for $A=C(X)$ and amenable $G$ the condition is equivalent to almost finiteness of $G\curvearrowright X$.

title: Marcelo Laca (joint with Camila F
note: Marcelo Laca (joint with Camila F. Sehnem), constructible right ideals and foundation-set relations give the full boundary quotient of a semigroup Toeplitz algebra and a criterion for its reduced quotient to be purely infinite simple. Key computation: for $P\subseteq G$, neutral words $\alpha$ produce projections $L_{\dot\alpha}=1_{K(\alpha)}$, and adjoining $\prod_{\beta\in F}(w_{\dot\alpha}-w_{\dot\beta})=0$ for every foundation cover $\bigcup_{\beta\in F}K(\beta)\subseteq K(\alpha)$ yields canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal C\rtimes_{\mathcal C P}P\cong C^*(w_p\mid\mathrm{(T1)-(T5)})\cong C(\partial\Omega_P)\rtimes_u G$; boundary topological freeness, equivalently condition $\mathrm{(BTF)}$, then makes $C(\partial\Omega_P)\rtimes_rG$ purely infinite simple, recovering this for $P=R\rtimes R^\times$ by explicitly choosing $s=(0,ac)$ or $s=(0,ac\bar x r)$ so that $psP\cap qsP=\varnothing$.

title: Gelu Popescu
note: Gelu Popescu, noncommutative Berezin kernels give a unique Wold decomposition and classify pure representations of the $C^*$-algebra of a noncommutative variety by multiplicity. Key computation: for $V_i=\pi(B_i)$ and $\Phi_{f,V}(Y)=\sum_{|\alpha|\ge1}a_\alpha V_\alpha YV_\alpha^*$, the projections $P_{\mathcal K_1}=\operatorname*{SOT-lim}_{s\to\infty}\Phi_{f,V}^s(I)$ and $P_{\mathcal K_0}=I-P_{\mathcal K_1}$ split $\mathcal K=\mathcal K_0\oplus\mathcal K_1$ into pure and Cuntz tuples; on $\mathcal K_0$, the constrained Berezin kernel is unitary and $V_i=K_{f,V,Q}^*(B_i\otimes I_{\mathcal D})K_{f,V,Q}$ with $\mathcal D=\operatorname{ran}(I-\Phi_{f,V})^m(I)^{1/2}$, so pure representations are unitarily equivalent exactly when $\dim\mathcal D$ agrees.

title: Leonel Robert
note: Leonel Robert, commutator subgroups of connected invertibles and unitaries in a unital $C^*$-algebra admit explicit exponential generators and strong simplicity properties. Key computation: the local Campbell--Baker--Hausdorff/Kashiwara--Vergne identities $e^xe^y=e^{x+y+[x,a]+[y,b]}$ and $e^{x+y}=(e^Re^xe^{-R})(e^Se^ye^{-S})$ show $e^{x+y}$ is commutator-equivalent to $e^xe^y$; consequently $D\mathrm{GL}_0(A)=\langle e^{[c,d]}:c,d\in A\rangle$ and $D\mathrm U_0(A)=\langle e^{i[x^*,x]}:x\in A\rangle$, and if $A$ has no one-dimensional representations then these groups are perfect, with $D\mathrm{GL}_0(A)$ generated by $1+x$ for $x^2=0$.

title: Camila F
note: Camila F. Sehnem (joint with Zahra Afsar, Marcelo Laca, and Jacqui Ramagge), the KMS$_\beta$ simplex of a Toeplitz noncommutative torus is classified by probability measures on a torus determined by the degeneracy of its zero-energy block. Key computation: for $r=(r_1,\ldots,r_k,0_d)$, every KMS state satisfies $\varphi(L_pL_xL_y^*L_q^*)=\delta_{p,q}e^{-\beta\langle p,r\rangle}\varphi(L_xL_y^*)$ and is obtained from a trace $\omega$ on $Q\mathcal T_r(\mathbb N^n,\sigma_\Theta)Q$ by $T_\beta(\omega)(X)=Z(\beta)^{-1}\sum_{l\in\mathbb N^k\times0_d}e^{-\beta\langle l,r\rangle}\omega(QL_l^*XL_lQ)$, where $Q=\prod_{j=1}^k(1-L_{e_j}L_{e_j}^*)$ and $Z(\beta)=\sum_pe^{-\beta\langle p,r\rangle}$; since traces on $A_{\Theta_d}$ are states on $Z(A_{\Theta_d})\cong C(\mathbb T^m)$, this gives $\operatorname{KMS}_\beta\cong\mathcal M_1(\mathbb T^m)$.

title: Sarah Reznikoff (joint with Jonathan Brown
note: Sarah Reznikoff (joint with Jonathan Brown, Adam Fuller, and David Pitts), regular ideals of a $C^*$-algebra are classified by invariant regular ideals of a regular subalgebra, and regular graph-algebra quotients preserve Condition (L). Key computation: for a regular inclusion $B\subseteq A$ with faithful invariant expectation $E:A\to B$ and regular ideal intersection property, $J\mapsto J\cap B$ and $K\mapsto J_K=\{a\in A:E(a^*a)\in K^{\perp\perp}\}$ are inverse Boolean-algebra isomorphisms between regular ideals of $A$ and invariant regular ideals of $B$; for graph algebras, $J=J^{\perp\perp}$ is equivalent to $p_w\in J\Longleftrightarrow(\forall v\in T(w))(\exists u\in T(v))\,p_u\in H(J)$, which forces every cycle of $E/J$ to retain an entrance and hence preserves Condition (L).

title: Paul Skoufranis
note: Paul Skoufranis, tracial inequalities completely characterize convex hulls of unitary orbits of self-adjoint elements in arbitrary unital $C^*$-algebras and extend to joint majorization of commuting tuples. Key computation: for self-adjoint $S,T\in A$, one has $S\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\mathcal U(T))$ exactly when $\tau((S-\alpha)_+)\le\tau((T-\alpha)_+)$ and $\tau((-S-\alpha)_+)\le\tau((-T-\alpha)_+)$ for every lower-semicontinuous trace $\tau$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb R$; in $M_n$, this is equivalent to $\sum_{k=1}^ma_k\le\sum_{k=1}^mb_k$ for ordered eigenvalues (equality at $m=n$), to $a=Xb$ for a doubly stochastic $X$, and to a unital trace-preserving completely positive map $\Psi$ with $\Psi(T)=S$.

title: Dan Ursu (joint with Shirly Geffen)
note: Dan Ursu (joint with Shirly Geffen), simplicity of reduced crossed products by FC-hypercentral groups is characterized by the absence of a central corner on which a finite-conjugacy element acts inner with centralizer-invariant implementer. Key computation: for a minimal action $\alpha:G\curvearrowright A$ with $G$ FC-hypercentral, $A\rtimes_rG$ is not simple exactly when there exist $t\in\mathrm{FC}(G)\setminus\{e\}$, a nonzero $t$-invariant $p\in Z(I(A))$, and $u\in\mathcal U(I(A)p)$ such that $\alpha_t|_{I(A)p}=\operatorname{Ad}(u)$ and $\alpha_s(p)=p,\ \alpha_s(u)=u$ for every $s\in C_G(t)$; this refines proper outerness on the injective envelope and is equivalent, for separable $A$, to an intrinsic obstruction on an essential $t$-invariant ideal $J\triangleleft A$ with an implementing unitary in $M(J)$.

title: Matthew Kennedy
note: Matthew Kennedy, noncommutative Choquet theory classifies operator systems by compact matrix-convex state spaces and characterizes those arising from $C^*$-algebras as noncommutative Bauer simplices. Key computation: matrix convexity closes $K=\coprod_nK_n$ under $\sum_i\alpha_i^*x_i\alpha_i$ whenever $\sum_i\alpha_i^*\alpha_i=I$, and evaluation gives the dual equivalence $S\cong A(K)$; every $x\in K_n$ has a maximal representing nc state $\mu:C(K)\to M_n$ with $a(x)=\int_Ka\,d\lambda$ supported on $\partial K$, while uniqueness of this maximal state is equivalent to $A(K)^{**}$ being a von Neumann algebra and to $A(K)\otimes_cT=A(K)\otimes_{\max}T$ for every operator system $T$; adding closed $\partial K$ characterizes precisely nc state spaces of unital $C^*$-algebras.

title: Kenneth R
note: Kenneth R. Davidson, free semigroup algebras admit a Lebesgue--von Neumann--Wold decomposition and are uniformly hyperreflexive. Key computation: on Fock space $\mathcal F_n^2=\ell^2(\mathbb F_n^+)$ the left shifts satisfy $L_i^*L_j=\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sum_iL_iL_i^*=I-\xi_\varnothing\xi_\varnothing^*$, while $\mathcal L_n'=\mathcal R_n$ and every $A\in\mathcal L_n$ has Ces\`aro-summed Fourier expansion $A\sim\sum_wa_wL_w$; the structure projection $P$ determined by $\bigcap_{k\ge1}\mathcal S_0^k=\mathcal WP$ splits an arbitrary free semigroup algebra into von Neumann and type-$L$ corners, and Kennedy's wandering-vector theorem for absolutely continuous representations yields $\mathcal S\simeq\mathcal L^{(\alpha)}\oplus\mathcal S_a\oplus\mathcal S_{vN}\oplus\mathcal S_d$, with every free semigroup algebra hyperreflexive with constant at most $6$.

title: Michael Brannan
note: Michael Brannan, complete quantum graphs have no finite classical coloring but have quantum chromatic number exactly $n^2$, and their coloring algebras possess strongly solid noninjective factor representations. Key computation: the algebra $\mathcal A(\operatorname{Hom}(QK_n,K_{n^2}))$ is generated by $p_{ij}^{(a)}$ with $p_{ij}^{(a)}p_{kl}^{(a)}=\delta_{jk}n^{-1}p_{il}^{(a)}$, $\sum_jp_{ij}^{(a)}p_{jk}^{(b)}=\delta_{ab}p_{ik}^{(a)}$, $\sum_ip_{ii}^{(a)}=n^{-1}1$, and $\sum_ap_{ij}^{(a)}=\delta_{ij}1$; any unitary error basis $\{u_a\}_{a=1}^{n^2}\subset U(M_n)$ gives the representation $p_{ij}^{(a)}\mapsto n^{-1}u_a^*e_{ij}u_a$, while the quantum Hoffman bound supplies the reverse inequality, proving $\chi_q(QK_n)=n^2$ whereas $\chi_{\mathrm{loc}}(QK_n)=\infty$; for $n\ge3$ the same universal algebra has a faithful trace whose GNS algebra is a strongly solid noninjective $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.

title: Ra\'ul E
note: Ra\'ul E. Curto (joint with In Sung Hwang and Woo Young Lee), Potapov's factorization theorem extends from matrices to rational two-sided inner operator-valued functions. Key computation: rationality is defined by the Hankel-kernel condition $\theta H^2(\mathbb T,E)\subseteq\ker H_{\Phi^*}$ for a finite Blaschke product $\theta$; if an inner $\Delta$ divides $\Theta=\theta I_E$, then $\Delta$ is a finite product of Blaschke--Potapov factors $b_\alpha P_M+(I_E-P_M)$, and the Beurling--Lax--Halmos identity $\ker H_{\Phi^*}=\Delta H^2$ yields the coprime factorization $\Phi=\Delta A^*$; consequently a two-sided inner $\Phi\in H^\infty(\mathbb T,B(E))$ is rational exactly when it is a finite Blaschke--Potapov product.

title: Ryan O'Loughlin
note: Ryan O'Loughlin, compact truncated Toeplitz operators on a model space have continuous inner-multiple symbols exactly under the same conditions that give bounded symbols for all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators. Key computation: for $K_I^2=H^2\ominus IH^2$ and $A_g^I f=P_I(gf)$, the projective product space $X=\{\sum_kx_ky_k:\sum_k\|x_k\|_2\|y_k\|_2<\infty\}$ satisfies $X^*=\mathcal T(I)$ and ${}^*X=\mathcal T_c(I)$; the maps $S:X\to zH^1\cap K_{I^2}^1$, $f\mapsto If$, ${}^*S:C(\mathbb T)/(F_{I^2}\cap C(\mathbb T))\to\mathcal T_c(I)$, $[f]\mapsto A_{If}^I$, and $S^*:L^\infty/Q\to\mathcal T(I)$ identify their images with compact operators having symbols in $I C(\mathbb T)$ and bounded-symbol operators, so duality gives $\mathcal T_c(I)=\{A_{Ih}^I:h\in C(\mathbb T)\}$ if and only if every bounded $A_g^I$ has a bounded symbol.

title: Alfons Van Daele
note: Alfons Van Daele, the polar decomposition of the antipode determines the modular structure of a locally compact quantum group and proves uniqueness of Haar weights. Key computation: regular representations satisfy $\Delta(x)=W^*(1\otimes x)W$ and $(\Delta\otimes\iota)W=W_{13}W_{23}$, while the closed antipode has $S((\iota\otimes\omega)W)=(\iota\otimes\omega)W^*$ and polar decomposition $S=R\tau_{-i/2}$; for two left Haar weights, $(K\otimes T_r)W_1=W_2^*(K\otimes T_r)$ implies $(1\otimes u_t)W_1(1\otimes u_t^*)=W_1$, hence $\Delta(u_t)=1\otimes u_t$ and $u_t$ is scalar, proving uniqueness up to scale; relative modular theory then produces the affiliated modular element $\delta$ with $\psi=\varphi(\delta^{1/2}\,\cdot\,\delta^{1/2})$, $\Delta(\delta)=\delta\otimes\delta$, and $\sigma_t'(x)=\delta^{it}\sigma_t(x)\delta^{-it}$.

title: Jingbo Xia
note: Jingbo Xia, the Drury--Arveson space is the universal dilation space for commuting row contractions and its multiplier norm gives the correct multivariable von Neumann inequality. Key computation: for a strict commuting row contraction $A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)$, the identity $\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb Z_+^n}\frac{|\alpha|!}{\alpha!}A^\alpha(I-\sum_iA_iA_i^*)A^{*\alpha}=I$ makes $Zx=\sum_\alpha\frac{|\alpha|!}{\alpha!}(I-\sum_iA_iA_i^*)^{1/2}A^{*\alpha}x\,\zeta^\alpha$ an isometry into $H_n^2\otimes H$ satisfying $Zp(A^*)=(p(M_\zeta^*)\otimes I)Z$; hence $\|p(A)\|\leq\|p\|_{\operatorname{Mult}(H_n^2)}$, while for $\theta(\zeta)=\zeta_1\cdots\zeta_n$ one has $\|\theta^k\|_\infty=n^{-kn/2}$ but $\|\theta^k\|_{H_n^2}=((k!)^n/(nk)!)^{1/2}\asymp k^{(n-1)/4}n^{-kn/2}$, explicitly showing why the supremum norm cannot replace the multiplier norm for $n\ge2$.

title: Ilijas Farah
note: Ilijas Farah, set-theoretic saturation sharply classifies ultrapowers of separable $C^*$-algebras: CH makes all nonprincipal ultrapowers isomorphic, while failure of CH yields the maximal number of isomorphism types.
